### G177 - the round trip's five comparisons, with what each one cannot see - and the row-to-check mapping is this writer's INTERPRETATION of the brief's table, not a transcription

`lib/schgen/gates/round-trip.ts` reports spec §2's contract as five lists plus a sixth that is
explicitly not a pass. **Each is driven red on its own**, by deleting its reporting line and
watching exactly one named test fail (Task 11, Step 8; all six restored, `git status --porcelain`
clean). **What a green result does NOT mean, per comparison:**

| comparison | what it compares | what it cannot see |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `componentIdentity` | the designator SET, both directions, plus an unannotated `R?` | nothing about what any component IS |
| `pinIdentity` | the SYMBOL each designator is drawn with (`libId`'s entry name against the netlist's `libsource` part), and the exact set of pin numbers the export puts on a net | **a pin FUNCTION.** `importNetlist` does not read a node's `pinfunction`, so a symbol that keeps its lib id and has its pin NAMES edited is invisible here. Gate 6 is what compares a symbol's pin names against a datasheet table. |
| `netMembership` | the partition of sorted `designator.pin` sets as a MULTISET, with each not-connected pin a one-member set | **net NAMES, by design.** An interface net renamed with its topology intact passes. Gate 3 is what compares names, and is strictly stronger. |
| `values` | designator -> value, for every part in the model | |
| `footprints` | designator -> footprint, **for every part that declares one** | a part that declares none, which is the next row |
| `footprintsUndeclared` | the labels of parts with an empty `footprint` | it compares NOTHING; it is the list of things not compared |

**THE INTERPRETATION, stated because a later reader would otherwise take it for the brief's.** The
brief's table justifies the pin-identity row with *"pad-count parity cannot catch a swapped
IN/OUT"*. Given only an `ImportedNetlist`, the netlist's only record of which pins a designator
has and what they mean is its `libsource`, so this implementation reads the row as **the symbol
identity plus the pin-number set**. A swapped IN/OUT achieved by crossing two WIRES is caught by
`netMembership` instead; a swapped IN/OUT achieved by placing a different symbol with the same
numbering is caught by `pinIdentity`; **a swapped IN/OUT achieved by editing pin names inside one
symbol file is caught by NEITHER.** That third case is the residual.

**AND THE TWO WARNINGS ARE IN THE MODULE COMMENT, where an implementer reads them**, not only
here: a certificate verifies what it was given, not what you meant - everything here is
self-consistency between a drawing and the model it was drawn from, and the link that checks the
MODEL against an authored schematic is the committed-netlist comparison, not this; and a schematic
can export a correct netlist while visually suggesting wrong connections, so **the round trip is
not a readability gate and must never be reported as one.**

**AMENDED 2026-10-20 BY THE TASK 11 REVIEW, WITH THE THING THIS TABLE SAID IT COULD NOT SEE AND
DID NOT NAME: THE BRIEF'S OWN EXAMPLE.** Spec 2's component-identity row is justified by
*"two components swapped consistently produce the same partition"*, and the brief's Step 2 gave a
literal test for it - `netMembership` empty, `componentIdentity` non-empty. **This implementation
compares designator SETS, which cannot report a consistent swap at all.** The review measured it;
this writer then re-drove it over the real generated `mini` design rather than a synthetic circuit,
in three arms:

| arm | swap | `roundTrip`'s answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A** `C3`/`C4` - the two 100n decoupling caps, both `3V3`-to-`GND` | consistent, in `components[]` AND in every net | **ALL SIX LISTS EMPTY** |
| **B** `C1`/`C2` - 10u on `VIN` against 22u on `3V3` | the same transformation | `netMembership` 4 problems, `values` 2 - **`componentIdentity` empty** |
| **C** what distinguishes arm A's pair in the netlist at all | - | **nothing.** Their component records are identical apart from the designator, and their net sets are equal |

**ARM C IS THE ANSWER, AND IT MAKES THE SPEC'S EXAMPLE UNACHIEVABLE RATHER THAN MERELY UNMET.**
A consistent swap preserves the partition **only when the two components are indistinguishable in
the netlist** - same value, same footprint, same `libsource`, same net set. That is exactly the
case in which the netlist carries no information telling them apart, so **no function of
`ImportedNetlist` can report it**: not `componentIdentity` widened, not anything. And in that case
the swap is electrically a no-op, because the parts are interchangeable. The moment they differ at
all, the swap is caught - by `values`, `footprints`, `pinIdentity` or `netMembership`, as arm B
shows. **So the five rows TOGETHER catch every consistent swap of distinguishable components, and
the one case none of them catches is the one that is not a defect.**

**THIS WRITER'S POSITION, stated because the review asked for it and because the decision is not
the producing agent's to make: the row should NOT be widened, and the SPEC'S EXAMPLE IS WRONG** -
specifically its inference, not its premise. The premise (*a consistent swap preserves the
partition*) is true. The inference (*therefore a separate component-identity comparison is what
catches it*) does not follow, because the indistinguishability that blinds the partition blinds
every other netlist-derived comparison too. `componentIdentity` should keep the designator-set
claim, which has teeth of its own and its own perturbation.

**AND THE REAL GUARD AGAINST A MIS-ASSIGNED DESIGNATOR IS GATE 1, NOT THIS - which is the part a
later reader cannot re-derive.** `roundTrip` takes `refs` from the generation itself
(`g.annotation.refs`), so a generator that bound part labels to designators differently would
change both sides of the comparison and stay invisible here. What pins that binding is the
COMMITTED reference lock: `lib/schgen/lock/annotate.ts`'s `annotate` takes every already-locked
part's designator straight from `refs.lock.json` (lines 89-92, read directly), and gate 1's
`staleFiles` fails when the regenerated lock differs from the committed one by content. **A
designator swap is a gate-1 finding.**

**A SECOND THING THE REVIEW FOUND, and it is the same residual class as G174 and G171:
`roundTrip` HAS NO CONSUMER OUTSIDE ITS OWN TEST.** `runGates` registers gates 1, 3, 6, 7 and 8 -
not the round trip - so this task's headline deliverable executes only on the ported `mini`
fixture, never through `make check` over a design, and never on a circuit in `circuits/`.
Measured on the IMPORT rather than on the identifier, because the identifier is ambiguous:
`grep -rln "gates/round-trip.ts" lib tools tests --include="*.ts"` returns **exactly one file**,
`tests/schgen/gates/round-trip.kicad.test.ts`. (A grep for the bare name `roundTrip` would NOT
have settled it - `tests/stripboard/vero-export-fixtures.ts` exports an unrelated `roundTrip` for
VeroRoute documents, with three more call sites in `vero-export.test.ts`. The first version of
this sentence cited that grep, and it would have been wrong.) The brief did not ask for it to be
registered, so this is not a compliance miss - but **Tasks 18 and 19 both rest on it**, and
leaning on a check that has never run inside the pipeline is the thing worth knowing first.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 11, Steps 6 and 8. **Amended the same day by the Task 11 review**,
  which drove the consistent-swap case and the no-consumer grep.
- **Evidence** the six perturbations, each turning exactly one named test red:
  deleting `componentIdentity`'s schematic-side push fails *"a component the schematic has and the
  model does not is caught by component identity alone"* (6 pass / 1 fail); the symbol comparison
  fails *"the wrong symbol under the right designator is caught by pin identity, not by the
  partition"*; the partition's two pushes fail *"a pin moved between two nets is caught by net
  membership alone"*; the value comparison fails *"a wrong capacitor on a correct topology is
  caught by values alone"*; the footprint comparison fails *"a wrong footprint on a correct symbol
  is caught by footprints alone"*; and `footprintsUndeclared.push` fails *"a component with no
  declared footprint is reported, not passed"*. Each restore was verified by SHA-256 and the final
  `git status --porcelain` was empty. For the residual, a check that could have failed:
  `grep -c "pinfunction" lib/kicad/netlist.ts` returns **0**. **For the consistent-swap arms
  above:** arm A exchanges `C3` and `C4` in `components[]` and in every net member of the real
  generated `mini` export and `roundTrip` returns six empty lists; arm B does the identical
  transformation to `C1`/`C2` and returns
  `values: ["C1: the schematic says \"22u\" and the model says \"10u\"", "C2: the schematic says
  \"10u\" and the model says \"22u\""]` plus four `netMembership` problems and an empty
  `componentIdentity`; arm C prints `identical apart from the designator: true` and
  `same net set: true` for arm A's pair. A check that could have failed and did: arm A was run
  first expecting `componentIdentity` to fire.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer wrote and ran the perturbation harness and read its output.
- **Why it is open** the `pinfunction` residual needs `importNetlist` to read a field it does not
  read, which is a change to a hand-written module four other consumers share, and no brief asks
  for it. The consistent-swap row is open as a QUESTION FOR THE SPEC'S AUTHOR rather than as work:
  this writer's position is above, and an agent producing the artifact may not settle its own
  acceptance criteria. The no-consumer residual is open because registering the round trip in
  `runGates` is a scope decision, and the gate it would join cannot run on any circuit here
  anyway (**G178**).
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: a generated schematic whose symbol has two pin NAMES
  exchanged, with its lib id, pin numbers, values, footprints and every net membership unchanged,
  is reported by something - and the test that proves it could have failed.** **MECHANISM,
  untried:** have `importNetlist` carry each node's `pinfunction` and have `roundTrip` compare it
  against `IrPin.identity`.

  **THE MECHANISM IS CHEAPER THAN THIS ENTRY FIRST IMPLIED, AND IT IS ALSO NOT A PLAIN EQUALITY -
  both measured 2026-10-20, and the second correction is the one that would have made an
  implementer ship a non-fix.** Cheap: KiCad DOES emit the field, so widening `importNetlist` is
  additive parsing and not a format change - **32** `pinfunction` atoms in a fresh s-expression
  export of the generated `mini` design, and **21** in the committed hand-drawn
  `tests/fixtures/pt2399-core.net` (44 in `transistor-preamp-lab.net`). The expensive part is only
  that four consumers share the module.

  **Not a plain equality:** every one of those atoms is `<symbol pin name>_<pin number>`, never
  the bare name. Counted over the generated export, **32 of 32 end in `_<pin>` and 0 do not**;
  `J2.7 -> "Pin_7_7"` is the giveaway, and the hand-drawn stub agrees at **21 of 21**
  (`U1.1 -> "VCC_1"`, `U1.3 -> "AGND_3"`). So a comparison against `IrPin.identity` - which holds
  `"VCC"`, `"+"`, `"GND"` - **would fail on every pin** unless the `_<pin>` suffix is stripped
  first. And the field is **absent** for a pin the symbol does not name: 24 of 56 nodes in the
  generated export, 44 of 65 in the stub, so the comparison covers only the named-pin subset and
  must say so rather than treating an absent field as agreement.

  **AND A SUB-QUESTION THAT SHOULD BE ANSWERED BEFORE TASK 18 OR 19 LEANS ON THE ROUND TRIP:**
  whether gate 6 already discharges this criterion depends on whether the IR's `identity` derives
  from the same symbol file the drawing places. If it does, gate 6's datasheet-table comparison
  catches the pin-name edit by a different route and no widening is needed; if it does not, the
  two checks are measuring different things and the gap is real. **Nobody has established which.**

### G178 - measured: gate 1 refuses on all FOUR parity circuits and gates 3 and 6 therefore run on none of them - and the refusal counts agree exactly with the ones already pinned, plus one

`tools/schgen/gate-census.ts` assembles a `LoadedDesign` per parity circuit from its authoring
declaration and runs the real `runGates`. **The result, for every one of the four: gate 1 refuses,
gates 3 and 6 report `not run: generation was refused`, and gates 7 and 8 are not registered at
all.**

| circuit | gate 1 | gate 3 | gate 6 | gate 7 | gate 8 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `opamp-buffer` | 40 | 1 (cascaded) | 1 (cascaded) | not registered | not registered |
| `optical-compressor` | 163 | 1 (cascaded) | 1 (cascaded) | not registered | not registered |
| `pt2399-core` | 115 | 1 (cascaded) | 1 (cascaded) | not registered | not registered |
| `transistor-preamp` | 101 | 1 (cascaded) | 1 (cascaded) | not registered | not registered |

**WHY THAT IS THE CORRECT RESULT AND NOT A DEFECT.** `generate` calls `validateCircuit` and
throws, and **G151** already measured that `circuitSpecFrom`'s output does not pass it: passing
would need an invented net rename (**G150**), an invented no-connect reason (**G151**) and
invented BOM fields (**G149**), and *"no backend invents an input"*. The census calls
`validateCircuit` through `generate` exactly as `make check` would, relaxes no rule, and supplies
no value the model does not hold.

**THE CROSS-CHECK, which is this entry's own evidence that the numbers are not made up.**
`tests/schgen/authoring-complete.test.ts` already pins the per-circuit `validateCircuit` totals as
**39 / 162 / 114 / 100**. The census reports **40 / 163 / 115 / 101** - exactly one more each, and
the one is `generate`'s `"circuit is invalid:"` header line, which the census classifies as
`header` and counts. Two independently-written measurements of the same thing agree, and the
difference is explained rather than waved at.

**PER-CLASS, with the four rule classes transcribed from that test's own `RULE_CLASSES` rather
than re-worded:**

| circuit | header | netNames (G150) | pinsDeclared (G151) | singlePinNets (G159) | bomFields (G149) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `opamp-buffer` | 1 | 0 | 3 | 0 | 36 |
| `optical-compressor` | 1 | 14 | 0 | 0 | 148 |
| `pt2399-core` | 1 | 17 | 0 | 1 | 96 |
| `transistor-preamp` | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 100 |

**BOM FIELDS ARE 380 OF THE 419 REFUSALS - 91%.** That is one finding, not four hundred: the
circuit model has no BOM, so `from-network.ts` emits empty `Manufacturer`, `MPN`, `Supplier` and
`SupplierPart` for every part, and `validateCircuit` refuses each field of each part separately.
**G149** is the entry; what this measurement adds is the scale, and that **gate 3 and gate 6
cannot be exercised on a single one of this repository's own circuits until it is resolved.** The
only circuit either gate has ever run on is the ported `mini` fixture, which carries a test BOM.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 11, Step 7.
- **Evidence** `bun run tools/schgen/gate-census.ts`, whose output is quoted above and whose
  classifier prints any unmatched refusal in full under `other:` - so the fifth class

  `tests/schgen/authoring-complete.test.ts`'s `EXPECTED_REFUSALS`, which is a committed assertion
  written by a different task - they agree on all four, off by the one header line.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer wrote the census, ran it, and compared its output against
  the committed expectations line by line.
- **Why it is open** the three inventions are forbidden and the model has nowhere to put the three
  things. Each has its own entry and its own mechanism; this entry exists for the CONSEQUENCE,

- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: gates 3 and 6 run - registered, and reporting a problem

### G179 - commit `84e00f1` left the full suite RED, and a SCOPED GREEN RUN in its message is what made that invisible - the shape, not the one commit, is the finding

**THE INSTANCE.** Task 11's first commit, `84e00f1`, added
`tests/schgen/gates/pin-identity.test.ts` and `pin-table.test.ts`. Their fixtures declare literals
that three repo-wide static sweeps reject - `Pkg:SOIC8`, `Pkg:MISSING`, `Pkg:TWO`,
`Pkg:SOIC8EP`, a bare `" "`, and the lib ids `Fix:OPAMP2`, `Fix:OPAMP2X`, `H7:TPS7A4901` - and
**every exemption those literals need landed one commit later, in `debf443`.** So `bun test` was
red at `84e00f1`, which breaks the standing constraint that **`bun test` is green at every
commit** and the posture behind ruling R4 (never land red). It was fixed in the next commit.

**MEASURED, not inferred.** With the three guard files reverted to the content `84e00f1` left them
at and everything else at `HEAD` - the sweeps are static over file text, so this reproduces that
commit's guard outcome - `bun test tests/kicad/footprint-names.test.ts tests/kicad/symbol-names.test.ts`
gives **12 pass / 3 fail**:

```
(fail) every symbol name swept out of the source resolves in an installed KiCad library
(fail) every footprint name swept out of the repository resolves in an installed KiCad library
(fail) every swept value that is not a KiCad lib id is one this repository has accounted for
  error: symbol library for "H7:TPS7A4901" is not at .../SharedSupport/symbols/H7.kicad_sym
  +   "Pkg:SOIC8 (tests/schgen/gates/pin-identity.test.ts)",
  +   "Pkg:MISSING (tests/schgen/gates/pin-identity.test.ts)",
  +   "Pkg:TWO (tests/schgen/gates/pin-identity.test.ts)",
  +   "Pkg:SOIC8EP (tests/schgen/gates/pin-identity.test.ts)",

```

Each failure names the file that landed in `84e00f1`. The commit boundary is checkable too:
`git log --diff-filter=A -- tests/schgen/gates/pin-identity.test.ts` gives `84e00f1`, and
`git log 84e00f1..debf443 -- tests/kicad/footprint-sweep.ts tests/kicad/footprint-names.test.ts tests/kicad/symbol-names.test.ts`
gives `debf443` for all three, with `84e00f1` touching none of them.

**THE SHAPE, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS AN ENTRY AND NOT A NOTE ON ONE COMMIT.** `84e00f1`'s message
reports what was actually run:

> *"90 ported gate tests pass; `bun run typecheck` clean; 726 tests across tests/schgen/ pass."*

**Every one of those numbers is true, and none of them is the suite.** The implementer ran
`bun test tests/schgen/gates/`, then `bun test tests/schgen/port-fidelity.test.ts`, then
`bun test tests/schgen/` - three scoped runs over the directory being worked in - and committed.
The three sweeps that broke live in `tests/kicad/`, which no scoped run touched. **A scoped green
run reported in a commit message where a full run would have been red is indistinguishable, to a
reader of the history, from a commit that was green** - and it is more convincing than silence,
because it carries numbers.

**AND IT IS THE PREDICTABLE FAILURE MODE OF THIS PARTICULAR PORT**, which is what makes it worth
anticipating rather than merely regretting: **G176** records that the port now holds exemptions in
five tables across four guard files, all of them under `tests/kicad/` and
`tests/stripboard/` - that is, all of them OUTSIDE the directory a schgen task works in and runs
its scoped tests over. **G133** said the recurrence matters more than any one exemption; this is
the recurrence biting the commit cadence rather than the code.

- **Found** 2026-10-20 by the Task 11 review, which read the commit sequence. The implementer had
  observed the three failures during the task (they are quoted in **G176**'s evidence as
  *"3290 pass / 3 fail the moment the ported gate tests entered the tree"*) and fixed them, but
  observed them at a LATER, uncommitted tree state and never established that `84e00f1` itself was
  red - so the constraint breach went unrecorded while the symptom was recorded twice.
- **Evidence** the reverted-guard measurement above, the two `git log` queries, and `84e00f1`'s own
  message quoted verbatim. A check that could have failed: the revert harness restored all three
  files and verified each by SHA-256, and `git status --porcelain` afterwards showed only the
  register edit in flight.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer ran the revert measurement and both `git log` queries.
  **RELAYED for the discovery itself**, which was the review's.
- **Why it is open** the red commit is history and cannot be made green without rewriting it,
  which is not worth it on a pushed branch; the branch is green at its head and at every commit
  after `84e00f1`. What is open is the SHAPE: nothing stops the next task doing the same thing, and
  the scoped-run habit is otherwise good practice (it is fast, and it is what makes
  commit-early-often workable).
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: a commit that leaves `bun test` red cannot be pushed
  without someone knowing it is red.** Note what this deliberately does NOT say: it does not
  require a full suite run before every commit, because that would fight the commit cadence
  `AGENTS.md` requires, and it does not forbid reporting a scoped run.
  **MECHANISMS, both untried, and NOT a git hook** - `CLAUDE.md` forbids those outright
  (*"No git hooks, ever"*), so the obvious answer is ruled out before it is proposed.
  (1) **A CLI verb**, which is where `CLAUDE.md` says enforcement belongs: a `make check-full` or
  `bun run check` invocation that a task runs once before PUSHING rather than before each commit -
  cheap, because a push is less frequent than a commit, and it bounds the red window to one
  unpushed stretch rather than eliminating it.
  (2) **State the scope in the message**, so a scoped run cannot read as a full one: a commit
  reporting test numbers names the command that produced them. This commit's message did name
  them (*"726 tests across tests/schgen/"*), which is why the review could tell - so the mechanism
  is partly already in force by habit, and making it a rule costs nothing.
  **A THIRD, for the specific recurrence rather than the general shape:** have a schgen task's
  scoped run include `tests/kicad/` and `tests/stripboard/temp-scratch.test.ts` by default, since
  **G176** establishes that those are precisely the files a ported fixture breaks. That is the
  narrowest fix and the one that would have caught this instance.

### G180 - every spike figure now carries a SECOND caveat: this driver is not `netlistsvg`, and three specific numbers were properties of its skin

Task 12 lands the ELK backend, and **it does not drive ELK through `netlistsvg`.** Both spikes
did - `docs/schematic/elk-spike.md` and `docs/schematic/elk-block-spike.md`, through
`netlistsvg` at `d3518f1` with its pinned `elkjs` 0.7.1 - so every figure in **G94** through
**G101** was taken with a skin in the loop that this pipeline does not have. **G101** already
carries this caveat for its own floor; this entry carries it for the rest, and names the three
places the skin is demonstrably the cause rather than a confound.

| the spikes, through `netlistsvg` | here, measured | consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a node's size is a skin template's declared extent, resized by the skin | `u.symbol.boxes.get(u.unit)` placed at rotation 0, in micrometres | crossing counts depend on node size, so **G96**'s and **G100**'s numbers are not comparable |
| a declared port is a drawn 30x20 `inputExt` CELL | a boundary node of **width 0, height 0** | **G101**'s floor and its *"port glyphs are 10-67 % of a block's cells"* do not apply |
| the x-offset between congruent blocks is predicted by `6 * len(id) + 5`, the skin's 0.6 em at 10 px monospace (**G97**) | nothing in this graph draws a component id | **measured gone** - see **G185** |
| `elk.direction = DOWN`, the analog skin's | `RIGHT`, plan decision **D4** | D4 states this cost itself |

**AND ONE THING THIS ENTRY DOES NOT CLAIM.** It does not say the spikes' numbers are wrong, and
it does not re-measure them. Task 17 is the re-measurement; `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-19-schematic-authoring-m1.md`
decision **D4** names §1.1, §1.8, §3.3 and §3.4 as the figures that may move.

**A SECOND, SMALLER ITEM BELONGS HERE because it is an interpretation and not a measurement.**
The Task 12 brief asks for `elk.spacing.nodeNode` and
`elk.layered.spacing.nodeNodeBetweenLayers` *"in whole grid steps"* and names no number.
`lib/schgen/elk/options.ts` takes them from the ported templates' own reviewed constants -

grounds that the templates are the reviewed human arrangement and ELK is the thing being made to
match them. **Which constant maps to which option is this writer's reading**: `columnXs` uses
`PITCH` as the minimum step between adjacent rung COLUMNS, which under `direction = RIGHT` is a
layer step, and `STUB` is the smallest reviewed non-unit spacing in the kit. Nothing in the spec

**AND A SECOND INTERPRETATION OF EXACTLY THE SAME CLASS SHIPPED UNREGISTERED IN ROUND 1, which

| | |
| --- | --- |
| boundary nodes across all twelve declared blocks | **38** |
| of them unconstrained | **34** |
| `LAST_SEPARATE` | **4** |
| `FIRST_SEPARATE` | **0** |

`[RAN]` And on a constructed probe with a non-rail inbound net, **`FIRST_SEPARATE`, `FIRST` and no

### G181 - `elkjs` stamps a GWT identity hash on the graph it returns, and its value depends on what the worker laid out BEFORE - so the raw returned object is not a function of the input

`[RAN]` `elkjs@0.9.3`'s returned `ElkNode` carries a `$H` property on the root, on every child and
on every edge. It is not in `elkjs`'s own `ElkNode` type; it is GWT's identity hash code, assigned
in sequence as the worker hashes objects. **It therefore depends on everything laid out before,
on the same worker.** Two blocks with the SAME graph in one `layoutBlocks` call:

```
FIRST   $H: 277 282 286 288 13
SECOND  $H: 371 375 379 381 369
```

So `JSON.stringify(outcome.graph)` is **not** a key for a drawing. `lib/schgen/elk/serialize.ts`
emits only declared keys, so `$H` never appears in it, and every determinism comparison in
`tests/schgen/elk/layout.elk.test.ts` goes through it.

**THIS DOES NOT CONTRADICT G95's DETERMINISM HALF, and the distinction is worth stating because it
is easy to mis-state in either direction.** G95: *"determinism for a FIXED input still holds - 14
of 14 inputs gave one distinct output over three runs."* That holds here too: `layoutBlocks`
builds one `ELK` per call, so a fresh worker starts a fresh hash sequence and three separate calls
on one input give three IDENTICAL raw strings. **The instability shows up only within a single
call over two or more blocks** - which is exactly how the pre-pass runs. An earlier probe in this
task measured 3 distinct of 3 by calling `layout` three times on ONE instance; that figure is
correct for that arrangement and is NOT what `layoutBlocks` does.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 12, Step 8, while writing the determinism test.
- **Evidence** `tests/schgen/elk/layout.elk.test.ts`'s test *"two identical graphs on one worker
  serialize alike and raw-stringify differently"*, which asserts BOTH halves - the serialized
  forms equal and the raw forms unequal - so it fails if either stops being true. The `$H` numbers
  above are from the probe that found it. A second test asserts the serialized output does not
  contain `$H` **and** that the raw object does, so neither half is a check of nothing.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer ran the probe and wrote both tests.
- **Why it is open** it is a property of the dependency, not a defect to fix here, and it is a trap
  for any later task that compares ELK output: Task 16's manifest and Task 17's re-measurement both
  compare drawings, and the obvious `JSON.stringify` is wrong for the reason above.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: every comparison of an ELK output goes through
  `serializeElkInput` (or another writer that emits only declared keys), never through
  `JSON.stringify` of the returned object.** Nothing needs fixing for that to hold today; what
  would break it is a later task reaching for the raw object. **MECHANISM, untried:** a guard that
  greps for `JSON.stringify` applied to an `ElkNode` would be a text sweep over a shape the type
  system already describes, so it is recorded as an option and not taken.

### G182 - two of Task 9's three rules key on `ComponentKind`, which the IR does not carry, so neither `pinSidesFor` nor `preferredOrientation` is callable from a `BlockSubgraph` - and the ELK graph is built in the library frame as a result

`[CODE]` `grep -rn "ComponentKind" --include="*.ts" lib/schgen` returns **15 lines: 13 in
`lib/schgen/rules/`** (`pin-sides.ts`, `orientation.ts`, `symbols.ts`) **and 2 in
`lib/schgen/elk/graph.ts`'s own doc comment**, which is this entry restated at the call site.
**Nothing under `lib/schgen/ir/` or `lib/schgen/render/` names the type at all.**
`ComponentKind` is declared in
`lib/model/types.ts` and reaches `lib/schgen/` only through `from-network.ts`, which holds the
`Network`. **`IrPart` has no kind field** - its fourteen fields are label, refPrefix, libId, units,
value, footprint, bom, dnp, checklist, source, pinTable, mechanicalPads, ncUnlistedReason, order -
and a `BlockSubgraph`'s units carry `IrPart`. So:

- **`pinSidesFor(kind, symbol)` cannot be called**, and `lib/schgen/elk/graph.ts` calls
  `sideOfPin(rot, pin)` instead. **That is the same rule, not a substitute, and the Task 12 review
  verified it line by line:** `pinSidesFor`'s whole body is
  `for (const pin of symbol.pins) sides.set(pin.number, sideOfPin(0, pin))` plus a refusal, `kind`
  is read **only to compose that refusal's message**, and the call here is *the identical
  expression, from the identical exported function in the identical reviewed module*. And
  `pin-sides.ts`'s own doc comment **prescribes** it: *"the rotated side is `sideOfPin(rot, pin)`
  at drawing time and is deliberately not baked in here."* The equivalent no-pin refusal is in
  `graph.ts`'s `libPinOf`, naming the part, the unit, the symbol and the pin number. **This half
  costs nothing measurable, G99 holds for sides, and the row in G99 stays settled.**
- **`preferredOrientation(kind, context)` cannot be called either, and this half DOES cost
  something.** `lib/schgen/elk/graph.ts` builds every node at `GRAPH_ROTATION = 0`. That is a
  stated frame - the orientation the symbol library itself draws the part in - and `pinEnd`,
  `placeBox` and `sideOfPin` are all applied through that one value, so spec §1.4 obligation 3's
  *"the transform is applied once, to the library pin geometry, and the result is what both ELK and
  the emitter see"* holds within this layer. **But spec §1.5's step-2 rule library never runs**, so
  a part whose grounded end the rule would have put at the bottom is not turned, and §1.5's step 3
  (*"ELK may choose among orientations the rules leave open"*) is not available either, because
  FIXED_POS needs a rotation fixed before the graph exists.

**AND THE GAP WIDENS AT `generate`, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS NOT ONLY ABOUT ONE SIGNATURE.**
`preferredOrientationsOf` - the rule's one existing consumer - takes a `Network`, and `generate`
never holds one: it holds a `LoadedDesign` whose `DesignSpec.circuit` is a `CircuitSpec`. So the
orientation map cannot be computed inside the pipeline as it stands, with or without a signature
change to `elkInputOf`.

**THE CONCRETE COLLISION THIS SETS UP IS TASK 13's, AND IT IS NOW RULED ON.** Its brief says
`adaptElkLayout` takes `rot` from `preferredOrientation`. A placement rotated after the ports were
fixed at rotation 0 is the SECOND transform obligation 3 forbids by name - *"the result is what
**both** ELK and the emitter see"* - and the wire attachment points would be computed from geometry
ELK never saw. **Controller ruling R29 (plan, Task 13) forbids it and takes mechanism 2 below:**
the orientation map is carried as derived data from `from-network.ts` onto `BlockUnit`, and the
ports are fixed at that rotation. The measurement that decided it: of 102 parts, **73 `null`, 28
rotation 0, and exactly ONE rotation 180** - so the rule moves one part in this repository today,
which is why mechanism 1's larger change was not needed.

**THIS ENTRY IS THE DETAIL; G99 IS THE INVENTORY.** **G99**'s table row for a drawn orientation
read *"settled"* and said nothing about the backend being unable to reach it, so a reader starting
there was told a closed question. That row now points here, and its pin-side row records that the
backend reaches the same rule as `sideOfPin(rot, pin)`. **Neither entry stands alone: G99 is where
someone looks to learn what a backend needs, and this is where the reason one input does not arrive
lives.**

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 12, Step 5, when the brief's *"`"elk.port.side"` from `pinSidesFor`"*
  turned out not to be callable.
- **Evidence** the grep above (15 lines, 13 of them in `rules/` and the other 2 a doc comment, none
  under `ir/` or `render/`); `IrPart`'s field list read
  directly in `lib/schgen/ir/types.ts`; `preferredOrientationsOf`'s signature in
  `lib/schgen/from-network.ts` (`network: Network`); and `generate`'s own parameter list. A check
  that could have failed: `bun run typecheck` fails if `graph.ts` tries to call either rule, which
  is how this was found rather than reasoned about.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer ran the grep, read the three files and hit the type error.
- **Why it is open** closing it is a change to the IR or to `generate`'s inputs, which is larger
  than Task 12 and lands in the middle of Task 13's obligations. Nothing is broken today: every
  block draws, and the drawing is in the library frame rather than in a wrong frame.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: the rotation a block's ELK ports are fixed at is the same
  rotation its placements are emitted at, and it is the one spec §1.5's authority order chooses.**
  Note what this does NOT say: it does not require rotation 0 to be replaced, only that the two
  agree and that the choice comes from §1.5 rather than from whichever module needed a number.
  **MECHANISMS, three, all untried and they disagree:** (1) carry a `ComponentKind` on `PartSpec`
  and `IrPart`, which makes all three rules reachable everywhere and is the largest change;
  (2) **TAKEN, by ruling R29** - compute the orientation map in `from-network.ts` (where the
  `Network` is) and carry it as derived data onto `BlockUnit`, which keeps the kind out of the IR
  but adds a derived map to it. **It is Task 13's work, not Task 12's**, and it is no longer
  untried-advice: the controller ruled on it with the 73/28/1 measurement in hand;
  (3) leave the graph in the library frame and make Task 13 emit placements at rotation 0 too,
  which satisfies the criterion trivially and gives up §1.5 step 2 - **and that is a decision about
  a drawing's semantics, so it is not Task 13's to make silently.**

### G183 - `elkjs`'s documented node entry point cannot construct an `ELK` under Bun, in every version from 0.9.3 to 0.12.0, and the reason is that Bun defines a global `self`

**THE FIRST RUNTIME DEPENDENCY THIS REPOSITORY HAS ADDED SINCE `eecircuit-engine`**, so what it is
and what it costs are recorded rather than left in `package.json`.

**WHAT WAS PINNED, AND WHY NOT THE LATEST.** `elkjs@0.9.3`, exactly (`bun add elkjs@0.9.3
--exact`). It is one of the two versions **G94** reproduced its crash on (*"elkjs 0.7.1 and 0.9.3
both raise"*), so Task 14's reproduction and G94's measurement are about the same build.
**The cost of that choice: 0.10.0, 0.10.1, 0.10.2, 0.11.0, 0.11.1 and 0.12.0 exist and none of
them has been evaluated here.** **Transitive cost: zero packages** - `elkjs` declares no runtime
dependencies, in 0.9.3 and in 0.12.0 alike. **On-disk cost: 7.7 MB in 12 files**, almost all of it
the GWT-compiled `lib/elk-worker.js` and `lib/elk-worker.min.js`. Licence **EPL-2.0**.

**STEP 1's PREMISE CHECK, AND IT FOUND NOTHING WRONG, WHICH IS WHY IT IS HERE.**
`elkjs@0.9.3` **does** ship `lib/elk-api.d.ts`, plus `lib/main.d.ts`, `lib/elk.bundled.d.ts` and
`lib/elk-worker.d.ts`, and `package.json` declares `"types": "lib/main"`. So no
`lib/schgen/elk/elkjs.d.ts` was written and no declaration file for an untyped dependency exists.
**And there is NO synchronous layout entry point**: the `ELK` interface's five members are
`layout`, `knownLayoutAlgorithms`, `knownLayoutOptions`, `knownLayoutCategories` and
`terminateWorker`, and every one but the last returns a `Promise`. `lib/elk-worker.min.js` exports
only its `FakeWorker` class. **So plan decision D2's premise holds and there is no deviation to
record** - which is the half of a premise check that gets forgotten.

**THE DEFECT.** `require("elkjs")` -> `lib/main.js` asks `lib/elk-worker.min.js` for its
`FakeWorker`, and that file chooses what to be with:

```js
if(typeof document===Yxe&&typeof self!==Yxe){var i=new h(self);self.onmessage=i.saveDispatch}
else if(typeof module!==Yxe&&module.exports){...module.exports={'default':j,Worker:j}}
```

(`Yxe` is `'undefined'`.) **Under Bun `typeof self` is `"object"` and `typeof document` is
`"undefined"`**, so the first branch wins: the module installs itself as a web worker, never
exports its class, and `main.js` then throws

```
TypeError: undefined is not a constructor (evaluating 'new _Worker(url)')
```

Importing that file directly also hangs, because it registers `self.onmessage` and runs
`gwtOnLoad`. **The branch is byte-identical in 0.9.3, 0.10.0, 0.11.0 and 0.12.0**, so no upgrade
fixes it.

**WHAT IS DONE INSTEAD, and it is `elkjs`'s own documented path rather than a workaround on the
library's internals.** `tools/schgen/elk/layout.ts` imports `ELK` from `elkjs/lib/elk-api.js` and
passes `workerUrl` plus a `workerFactory` that builds Bun's native `Worker`. Inside a real worker
`self` IS a worker scope, so the first branch above is the CORRECT one and the library works as
designed. The URL comes from `import.meta.resolve("elkjs/lib/elk-worker.min.js")` - owner ruling
**G169**: no path may be unique to one machine.

**No global is patched.** Deleting `globalThis.self` around the import would also work and was not
taken: it mutates a global for the lifetime of a module load, and a second library testing `self`
during that window would see the wrong answer.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 12, Step 1, on the first attempt to construct an `ELK`.
- **Evidence** the four version tarballs' `lib/elk-worker.min.js`, each grepped for the branch and
  each identical; the `TypeError` above, run; `typeof self === "object"` printed under
  `bun run`; and the `ELK` interface read in `lib/elk-api.d.ts`. A check that could have failed:
  `tests/schgen/elk/layout.elk.test.ts`'s first test reads the installed package's own
  `version` and compares it against `ELK_BACKEND`, so the pinned version and the string a refusal
  prints cannot drift; and 25 further tests in that directory lay out real graphs through the
  worker, which fail outright if the construction regresses.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer ran every measurement above.
- **Why it is open** it is a defect in a dependency and in Bun's globals, neither of which this
  repository fixes. It is recorded because the fix is non-obvious, because the obvious upgrade does
  not help, and because a future `bun` or `elkjs` release could change it in either direction.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: an `ELK` constructs and lays a graph out under the
  repository's own runtime, and the construction is checked by a test that fails when it stops
  working.** That is met today. What is NOT settled is whether the pinned version is the right one:
  **MECHANISM, untried:** run the four later versions against `tests/schgen/elk/` and against
  **G94**'s three arms, which is Task 14's or Task 17's measurement and not this task's - and
  **a version bump is a change to a measured baseline, not a maintenance chore.**

### G184 - the Task 12 brief's Step 9 names a test that CANNOT fail for the perturbation it describes, and a second reading of the same perturbation fails nothing at all

Step 9: *"Then reorder the serializer's keys; the byte-identity test goes red."*

**It does not.** The byte-identity test is *"two serializations of one input are byte-identical"* -
`serializeElkInput(graph)` compared with itself. Reordering a declared key list moves both sides of
that comparison together, so it stays green while **every hashed byte in the generation manifest
and every readability baseline taken against it changes.** That is the exact shape of a check that
cannot fail.

`[RAN]` What was done instead: `tests/schgen/elk/serialize.test.ts` pins one small graph's
serialization as a literal string, and THAT is what goes red.

| perturbation | byte-identity test | pinned-string test |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NODE_KEYS` `width`/`height` swapped | **green** (6 pass before, 5 pass after) | **RED**, printing both strings |
| `NODE_KEYS` `x`/`y` moved after `width`/`height` | green | **green** |

**THE SECOND ROW IS A FINDING IN ITS OWN RIGHT AND IT IS A LIMIT OF THE GOLDEN.** An input
graph's **nodes** carry no `x` or `y` - ELK assigns those - so reordering `NODE_KEYS`' `x` and `y`
changes no input serialization and nothing notices. The pinned string constrains a declared order
**only over the keys the input it pins actually carries.**

**TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE SENTENCE ABOVE AS FIRST WRITTEN, both from the Task 12 review, and the
second makes the gap WIDER than this entry claimed.** (1) It said `x` and `y` are *"keys only an
output carries"*, which is wrong at **port** level: a port's `x` and `y` are the pin end and are in
the pinned string, so `PORT_KEYS` IS constrained. It is `NODE_KEYS`' `x` and `y` that are not, and
the table row above was correctly scoped while the prose under it was not. (2) `[RAN]` Moving
`NODE_KEYS`' `x`/`y` after `width`/`height` gives **26 pass / 0 fail across all three
`tests/schgen/elk/` files** - so **the two ELK-output determinism comparisons are blind to it as
well**, not merely the golden. They compare one output against another output through the same
writer, which moves both sides together exactly as the byte-identity test does.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 12, Step 9, by running the perturbation the brief names.
- **Evidence** the two runs above, with their pass counts, and the failure output quoting the
  expected and received strings in full. A check that could have failed in the other direction: the
  first row's pinned-string test was green before the perturbation and red after, and green again
  after the restore. For the two corrections: the pinned string read directly (it carries
  `"x":1016,"y":0` on each port and no node-level `x`), and the whole-directory run at 26 pass /
  0 fail under the node-level reorder.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer ran all four states.
- **Why it is open** the brief's sentence is in `.superpowers/`, which is gitignored, so the entry
  is the only durable record; and the golden's blind spot is real and is inherited by every later
  task that edits the serializer.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: a change to any declared key order in
  `lib/schgen/elk/serialize.ts` turns a test red.** Met for every key the pinned input carries,
  **which includes a port's `x` and `y`**; **NOT met for `NODE_KEYS`' own `x` and `y`, nor for
  `bendPoints`, `sections`, `junctionPoints`, `incomingShape`, `outgoingShape`, `incomingSections`
  and `outgoingSections`**, which only a laid-out graph carries - and not met by the determinism
  comparisons either, for the reason in correction (2).
  **MECHANISM, untried:** pin a second golden over a LAID-OUT graph. The cost is that it pins
  `elkjs`'s geometry as well as this module's key order, so a version bump would move it - which is
  arguably correct (a moved baseline should be visible) and arguably noise. Deciding that is Task
  16's, which owns the manifest.

at the bottom - so this run is close to the all-vertical assignment, which is **the arm G94
predicts lays out.** It is consistent with G94 and establishes nothing about it.

Over all twelve blocks the 240 pin ports are **74 NORTH, 81 SOUTH, 27 EAST, 58 WEST**, and of the

**AND THE HORIZONTAL ARM IS NOW TRIED AND CLEAN, by the Task 12 review rather than by this

**THE CONGRUENCE RESULT, WHICH IS THE PART SOMEBODY WILL WANT TO ACT ON.** `circuits/transistor-preamp`
declares four structurally identical bias legs. **G97**'s amendment measured them at block scale
through `netlistsvg` and found every vertical offset, the internal vector and the starting corner
identical, with **one x difference predicted exactly by `6 * len(component id) + 5`** - the skin's

```
tp-leg-lower-a        JP3:1@(22,22) 10160x2286  R3:1@(15262,1810) 2032x7620  RV3:1@(22374,9450) 4826x7620

```

Nothing in this graph draws a component id, so the term that separated them is gone. **And
G97's second qualification is answered in the same run rather than left open:** it warns that
*"adding a rail symbol to one of two otherwise identical blocks stops them drawing alike"* -
`tp-leg-upper` runs from `VCC`, `tp-leg-lower-a` from `GND`, and under `netlistsvg`'s `v-rails`
that broke the congruence. Here a boundary net is a **zero-size node with no glyph**, so the two
still draw alike.

**WHAT THAT IS NOT.** It is **not** G97's re-measurement, for two reasons the entry itself gives:
no template is in the loop, and these blocks are drawn in ISOLATION rather than in sheet context.
It is also measured on node boxes, not on the drawn `.kicad_sch` - there is no drawing yet, because
the adapter is Task 13's.

**AND THE CONSEQUENCE TASK 16 NEEDS, which the congruence result makes easy to read the wrong way.**
`[RAN]` Those four byte-identical DRAWINGS have **four distinct SERIALIZATIONS**, so under spec
§2.1 they get **four distinct manifest keys**. The serialization is keyed by identity and not by
shape: node ids are `<designator>:<unit>`, port ids `<node>#<pin>`, edge ids `<net>:<index>` and a
boundary node is `port:<net>`, so the four differ in their designators (`JP1`/`R1`/`RV1` against
`JP2`/`R2`/`RV2`...), in their internal net names (`LOWER_A_FLOOR` against `LOWER_B_FLOOR`) and, for
two of the four, in a boundary net name (`port:VCC` and `port:COLLECTOR` against `port:GND`).
**Normalising designators and the block id still leaves four distinct strings**, because the net
names are genuinely different nets. **This is correct behaviour, not a defect** - two congruent
drawings of two different parts of a circuit are two drawings - but it means **a manifest cannot
recognise congruence, by construction**, and a later task must not expect it to.

**One mechanism offered for this was measured wrong and is recorded rather than repeated:** the
review attributed the distinctness to *"the two zero-size boundary nodes swapping order in
`children`"*. They do not swap - `boundaryNets` emits `g.rails` then `g.external`, and all four
legs come out `port:<rail-or-first-external> port:BASE` in that order. The cause is the identity
strings above, and the conclusion the review drew from it is right.

### G186 - making `generate` asynchronous cost THREE more byte-checked files, and the manifest's three lists are now 80 ported / 48 diverged / 61 hand-written

Plan decision **D2** puts the ELK layout in an asynchronous pre-pass inside `generate`. Threading
its result to the place it is used means touching the whole chain

```
generate -> layoutSheet -> blockContent -> renderBlock -> realiseBlock
```

and **three of those five modules were still byte-checked ports**. They are now `diverged[]`
entries with a `sourceSha`, which is ruling **R18** as extended:

| file | what changed | what it costs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tools/schgen/generate.ts` | `generate` is `async`; `GenerateEnv` gains `authoring`; `Generation` gains `elk`; `layoutSheet` is handed the backend | its MCU pin-map `cuts` (**G112**) are no longer carried as data - the deletions now live in the file |
| `lib/schgen/render/sheets.ts` | `layoutSheet` takes `elk: Backend \| null = null` and passes it on | one parameter |
| `lib/schgen/render/frames.ts` | `blockContent` takes `elk` and passes it on | one parameter |

`lib/schgen/render/bus.ts` and `tools/schgen/verify.ts` were already diverged; their `why` strings
are amended rather than re-stamped, because their pedals sources have not moved. **The counts
move from 83 / 45 / 52 to 80 / 48 / 61** (the nine new hand-written files are the three
`lib/schgen/elk/` modules, `tools/schgen/elk/layout.ts`, and five files under `tests/schgen/elk/` -
the fifth being `options.elk.test.ts`, added in review round 2 for **G187**).
**G139** is the entry that holds what a divergence costs: *"nothing compares a diverged file
against its source again."* Three more files are now in that state, and two of them -
`sheets.ts` and `frames.ts` - diverge by **one parameter each**, which is the worst ratio of
divergence cost to divergence content in the manifest so far.

**TWO SMALLER DECISIONS INSIDE THAT, BOTH RECORDED BECAUSE A READER WOULD ASK.**

**(a) `GenerateEnv.authoring` and not `DesignSpec.authoring` - AND ROUND 1's STATED REASON FOR IT
WAS HALF WRONG, which changes where the field belongs.** Round 1 said, here and in `generate.ts`'s
own comment, that `elkInputOf` needs **two** declared things the IR has no slot for -
`portDirections` and `rails`. **The rails half is already in the IR.** `BlockSubgraph.railSpecs` is
built by `subgraphOf` from `Circuit.rails`, keyed by exactly the `g.rails` set `boundaryNets` asks
about, with its own refusal when a rail has no spec - and a `RailSpec` carries `net`, `symbol`,
`kind` and `pwrFlag`, which is everything `negotiablePort` reads of it. So `elkInputOf` could have
served the rail half from its declared input, and **`elkInputOf`'s "undeclared rail" refusal can
only fire when a caller passes the WRONG circuit's authoring file** - which is a real check and is
now what that parameter buys, rather than the access it was said to provide.

**`portDirections` is the only input genuinely missing from the IR.** That is the whole of the
reason this field exists, and it relocates the fix: **a port direction belongs in the IR beside
`rails`**, not in `DesignSpec.authoring` and not on `GenerateEnv`. Ruling **R29** has Task 13
carrying the orientation map exactly that way - derived in `from-network.ts`, onto the IR - so the
precedent and the seam both exist.

The divergence of `generate.ts` was unavoidable regardless (`generate` had to become `async`), so
**the cost in the table above stands unchanged**. What would have misled a later agent is the
recorded reason, and that is what this correction is for. **The remaining cost is that a
design-data field rides on a type whose other four fields are environment**, which is the wrong
shape and is recorded as such.

**(b) `authoring: null` is passed by `tools/cli/schgen.ts` and by every design fixture, and it is
not a fallback.** No design module in this repository declares an authoring file, and every design
ported from `digital-pedal-platform` renders its blocks `wired` or `bus`, so the pre-pass has
nothing to do for them. A block that DOES select ELK with `null` refuses, naming the block and the
field. **`tools/schgen/gate-census.ts` passes the real thing** - each parity case's own
declaration - which changes no row today, because gate 1 already refuses on all four parity
circuits before the pre-pass runs (**G151**, **G178**).

**AND `generate` BEING ASYNC RIPPLED FURTHER THAN THE THREE.** `runGates` in
`tools/schgen/verify.ts` is now `async`; `gateCensus` in `tools/schgen/gate-census.ts` is now
`async` and builds its `GenerateEnv` per circuit rather than once; `runSchgen` awaits; and four
test files - `tests/schgen/emit-byte-stable.test.ts`, `tests/schgen/verify.test.ts`,
`tests/schgen/gates/gates.kicad.test.ts` and `tests/schgen/gates/round-trip.kicad.test.ts` -
await it across eleven call sites, with their enclosing `it`/`beforeAll` callbacks made `async`.
None of those four needed a new divergence: two were already diverged and two are hand-written.

### G187 - `elkjs` silently ignores an option key or value it does not recognise, so a typo in a layout option is invisible and would make the manifest certify the wrong drawing - now checked for KEYS, still open for ENUM VALUES

`[RAN]` On one probe graph with a non-rail inbound net, six arms of
`elk.layered.layering.layerConstraint`, compared on a geometry-only projection (every node's `x`,
`y`, `width`, `height` and every edge section's start, bend points and end; `layoutOptions`
excluded):

| arm | result |
| --- | --- |
| no constraint at all | baseline |
| `"FIRST_SEPARATE"` | **byte-identical to baseline** |
| `"FIRST"` | **byte-identical to baseline** |
| `"NOT_AN_ELK_VALUE"` | **byte-identical to baseline** |
| a misspelt KEY, `…layerConstraintt`, with a legal value | **byte-identical to baseline** |
| `"LAST_SEPARATE"` | **different** - the whole drawing moves |

**Six arms, two distinct geometries, and no raise or warning on any of them.** An extra
unrecognised key on the root graph (`elk.algorith`) is likewise accepted silently.

**WHY THAT IS A DEFECT HERE AND NOT JUST A LENIENT LIBRARY.** This backend emits **eight** option
strings, and two of this program's four measurements are taken against the drawing they produce:
**the generation manifest (spec §2.1) hashes the serialized input, and the readability baseline
(spec §3.3) is scoped to it.** A typo in any of the eight changes the drawing and nothing else -
no error, no log line - so **both would certify the wrong thing as the right thing, and the
manifest's whole purpose is to stop exactly that.** It is `CLAUDE.md`'s *"a skipped check must
never look like a passing one"* pointed at the options layer, and until review round 2 nothing in
this repository checked it.

**THE KEY HALF IS NOW CLOSED, by `tests/schgen/elk/options.elk.test.ts`.** It collects every
option key and value from a real block's graph - not from a hand-written list, so an option
`graph.ts` starts emitting is covered without anyone remembering - and asserts, against
`elkjs`'s own `knownLayoutOptions()` and `knownLayoutAlgorithms()`:

- every emitted key is a known option id;
- the option's `targets` includes the element kind it is attached to, because **an option on the
  wrong kind of element is ignored exactly as silently as a misspelt one**;
- `elk.algorithm`'s value is a known algorithm id;
- a numeric-typed option carries a finite number (both spacings are `DOUBLE`);
- and, as the anti-vacuity arm, that two deliberately misspelt ids are **not** in the vocabulary.

**THE REVIEW'S MECHANISM WAS HALF UNAVAILABLE, AND IT WOULD HAVE FAILED ON EVERY KEY AS WRITTEN -
which is this register's own "probe a mechanism before writing it down" rule, hit twice in one
finding.**

1. **The id form.** It asked that *"every emitted key appears in `knownLayoutOptions()`"*. `[RAN]`
   All **224** ids that call returns begin `org.eclipse.elk`, and **not one of the eight keys this
   backend emits is found by a literal lookup** - `elk.algorithm`, `elk.direction`,
   `elk.edgeRouting`, `elk.spacing.nodeNode`, `elk.layered.spacing.nodeNodeBetweenLayers`,
   `elk.portConstraints`, `elk.port.side` and `elk.layered.layering.layerConstraint` all return
   NOT FOUND. `elk.<rest>` is `elkjs`'s accepted shorthand for `org.eclipse.elk.<rest>`, and the
   expansion is the one translation the test performs. With it, **all eight resolve**, and every
   one is on the element kind `elkjs` targets it at:

   | emitted key | full id's `type` | `targets` | emitted on |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | `elk.algorithm` | STRING | PARENTS | root graph |
   | `elk.direction` | ENUM | PARENTS | root graph |
   | `elk.edgeRouting` | ENUM | PARENTS | root graph |
   | `elk.spacing.nodeNode` | DOUBLE | PARENTS | root graph |
   | `elk.layered.spacing.nodeNodeBetweenLayers` | DOUBLE | PARENTS | root graph |
   | `elk.portConstraints` | ENUM | NODES | every node |
   | `elk.port.side` | ENUM | PORTS | every pin port |
   | `elk.layered.layering.layerConstraint` | ENUM | NODES | a constrained boundary node |

2. **The value half cannot be done this way at all.** It asked for *"every value in its declared
   enum"*. `ElkLayoutOptionDescription` declares `id`, `name`, `description`, `group`, `type` and
   `targets` and **no choices**: `knownLayoutOptions()` reports that `elk.port.side` is an `ENUM`
   and will not say which strings are legal. A test asserts that - including that no returned field
   name contains "choice" or "value" - so if a later `elkjs` starts exposing them, the residue
   below is known to have changed shape rather than being silently still open.

**SO WHAT IS STILL OPEN IS FOUR ENUM VALUES**: `elk.direction = "RIGHT"`, `elk.edgeRouting =
"ORTHOGONAL"`, `elk.portConstraints = "FIXED_POS"` and `elk.port.side` in
`NORTH`/`SOUTH`/`EAST`/`WEST`, plus `elk.layered.layering.layerConstraint`'s two. **A typo in any of
those six is still invisible.** Three of them would be loud in practice - `FIXED_POS` is what makes
the drawing schematic-shaped at all (**G180**), `ORTHOGONAL` is what makes wires axis-aligned, and
`RIGHT` is decision **D4** - so a reader would notice; `elk.port.side` and `layerConstraint` would
not be noticed, and `layerConstraint` is measured above as producing the same drawing whether it is
legal or not.

- **Found** 2026-10-20 by the Task 12 review (Important 3), and the id-form and no-choices results
  by this writer while closing it.
- **Evidence** the six-arm geometry probe above and the 224-option vocabulary dump, both run here.
  **Checks that could have failed, driven:** perturbing `BLOCK_OPTIONS`'s `elk.edgeRouting` to
  `elk.edgeRoutingg` turns **two** tests in `options.elk.test.ts` red, one of them naming the key

  are NOT, so the vocabulary lookup cannot pass by finding nothing.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer ran the probes, wrote the test and ran the perturbation.
  **RELAYED for the discovery**, which is the review's.
- **Why it is open** the value half has no mechanism through `knownLayoutOptions()`, and the

  value - fails a check rather than changing a drawing.** Met for all eight keys and for the

  **which detects rather than prevents, and is a weaker reading of the criterion**, so it is
  offered as a mitigation and not as a settlement.

### G188 - ELK's UNSET spacing and padding defaults are absolute numbers in whatever unit the geometry is in, and this backend's unit is the MICROMETRE, so they are 0.8% of a grid step

`[RAN]` `tools/schgen/elk/graph.ts` hands `elkjs` two spacings, both whole grid steps
(`NODE_SEPARATION = STUB = 2 * GRID`, `LAYER_SEPARATION = PITCH = 4 * GRID`). **It hands it nothing
else, and every option it does not hand it keeps an ELK default that is a bare number** - padding
12, `spacing.edgeEdge` 10, `spacing.edgeNode` 10, `portPort` 10. The geometry in this backend is in
**micrometres**, so those defaults are 10-12 µm: **0.8 to 0.9 per cent of the 1.27 mm electrical
grid.**

**WHAT IT PRODUCES, measured on `dividerSubgraph` through the pinned `elkjs@0.9.3`:**

```
nodes   R_TOP:1 x 12 y 22    R_BOT:1 x 7124 y 7662    port:3V3 x 7124 y 12
edges   3V3:0  start (1028,22)  bend (1028,12)  end (7124,12)
```

The whole drawing sits at `(12, 22)` - ELK's default padding - and **every edge leaves its port with
a 10 µm jog** from the port's y to the padding line. Snapping a 10 µm segment onto a 1.27 mm grid
makes it zero length, which `snapToGrid` refuses as the identity collapse it is, so **every fixture
block refuses at spec §1.4 obligation 1.**

**THE DIAGNOSIS IS CONFIRMED BY A PROBE, NOT INFERRED.** The same five fixture blocks laid out twice
- once as shipped, once with `elk.padding` and the five remaining spacings at `GRID`:

| | shipped | spacings at whole grid steps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| blocks refusing at the snap gate | **5 of 5** | **0 of 5** |
| blocks drawing clean | 0 | 2 |
| blocks refusing at the clearance checks | 0 | 3 |

**THE OPTION VALUES ARE NOT CHANGED HERE AND THAT IS DELIBERATE.**
`lib/schgen/elk/options.ts`'s own header says *"nothing in this file was chosen because a drawing
looked better with it. Each value cites the decision, the specification clause or the ported
constant it comes from"*, and the Task 13 brief forbids tuning ELK options by name. The two spacings
that ARE set cite `STUB` and `PITCH`; **this writer has no reviewed source for a value for the other
six**, and picking one grid step because it makes the drawings appear is exactly the failure
`CLAUDE.md`'s governing invariant is about.

**AND IT IS WHY `graph.test.ts`'s SPACING ASSERTION IS NARROWER THAN IT READS.** That test says
*"both spacings are whole grid steps, which is what the plan asks both spacings to be"* - and its
reach is **the two options this backend sends**, while the sentence a reader takes from it is about
the spacings ELK USES. That is **G125**'s shape again: a guard whose reach is a fraction of its
claimed reach.

**ROUND 3: THE CAUSE IS SELF-LOOPS, THE OPTIONS ARE NOW SET, AND ROUND 2's CONCLUSION WAS WRONG
WHERE IT MATTERS.**

**Round 2 concluded that the criterion was *"necessary and NOT sufficient"*. That is wrong, and the
way it is wrong is this register's own worked example one layer up.** The criterion is *"every
spacing and padding `elkjs` uses is a whole number of grid steps"*, and round 2's probe arm set
**six of roughly thirteen**. It then measured a residue of 9 sub-grid segments and blamed the
criterion. **When the criterion is actually met, the residue is zero.** The criterion was right; the
instantiation was partial; the conclusion drawn was about the criterion.

**THE MISSING OPTION IS `elk.spacing.nodeSelfLoop`, AND IT HAS A NAMED CAUSE.** `edgesForNet` chains
a net of degree n into n-1 two-terminal edges, and when two consecutive terminals are pins of the
**same unit node** that chain edge is a **self-loop**, which `layered` routes with this option
alone - default **10**, in micrometres here.

`[RAN]` **Exactly 11 self-loops across 10 of the 12 blocks**, and their nets are exactly the nets
that carried the residual sub-grid segments:

| block | self-loops | on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ob-buffer` | 1 | `FB` on `U1:1` |
| `oc-power` | **0** | - |
| `oc-audio` | 2 | `MAKEUP_FB` on `J3:1`, `audio_BUF_OUT` on `U1:1` |
| `oc-sidechain` | 1 | `VBIAS` on `U2:2` |
| `pt-core` | 1 | `GND` on `U1:1` |
| the six `tp-leg-*` | 1 each | `BASE`/`GND`/`COLLECTOR` on `RV1`..`RV6` |
| `tp-stage` | **0** | - |

**The clincher: `oc-power` and `tp-stage` have zero self-loops, and they are precisely the two
blocks that cleared the snap gate before this option was set.** Not node size, not port position,
not edge count - a net with two terminals on one unit. A trimmer with its wiper tied to one end; an
op-amp with its output and inverting input on the feedback net.

**The three arms, measured:**

| arm | sub-grid segments | blocks carrying one | refuse at snap | refuse at obligation 2 | drawn |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ELK's defaults | **147 / 502** | 12 | 11 | 0 | 0 |
| six options, no `nodeSelfLoop` | 9 / 501 | 8 | 9 | 2 | 0 |
| **all seven** | **0 / 501** | **0** | **1** | **10** | **0** |

**A bisection over 14 unset candidates found only this one moves the count**:
`layered.spacing.baseValue`, `spacing.portsSurrounding`, `port.borderOffset`, `edge.thickness`,
`spacing.componentComponent`, `additionalEdgeSpacing` and every label and comment spacing leave it
unchanged.

**THE OPTIONS ARE NOW SET, UNDER AN EXPLICIT CONTROLLER SANCTION, AND THAT CHANGES A PIECE OF
EVIDENCE.** Task 12's review verified `lib/schgen/elk/options.ts` **byte-identical** as evidence
that no drawing had been tuned. **Round 3 changes that file**, so the byte-identity is spent and
must not be read as simply broken: this is a measured defect with a named cause, fixed under the
spec's own criterion, not an adjustment made until a drawing looked better. `GRID_SCALE_SPACINGS`
in that file carries the full argument. **The value question is untouched and stays open**: nothing
in the ported templates corresponds to *"the gap ELK leaves between an edge and a node"*, so there
is no reviewed constant to cite and `GRID` is used as the **smallest value satisfying the
criterion** - a stated rule, not a preference. Which reviewed constant should feed which option is
still nobody's answer (**G180**).

**AND THE BARRIER UNDER A FULLY-MET CRITERION IS NOT SNAP.** It is **obligation 2, on 10 of the 12
blocks** - which ruling **R33** then resolved by splitting at the branch point (**G199**). One block refuses at snap
(`oc-audio`, and it is the membership arm firing for the first time - **G196**) and one at
obligation 3 (`oc-sidechain`, **G190**). **Still 0 drawn and still no `PAIR_COVERAGE` pair fires.**

**This entry's own tripwire is spent and was replaced deliberately.** `options.elk.test.ts` pinned
four options as unset so that setting one without saying so would go red. It went red, as designed.
The test now asserts the criterion instead - every spacing-and-padding value sent is a whole number
of grid steps, the set sent is pinned, and `elk.spacing.nodeSelfLoop` is named because its absence
is the one nobody would guess at.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 13, while diagnosing why every block refused at the snap gate.
- **Evidence** the node and edge dump above, printed from a real `layoutBlocks` run; the two-arm

- **Why it is open** choosing a value for each option is choosing a layout option, which needs a
