### G189 - routing a net as a spanning CHAIN of two-terminal edges makes ELK retrace its own route, and every one of the 30 overlaps is a CONTAINMENT

**REWRITTEN 2026-10-20 AT ROUND 2. ROUND 1 CALLED THESE OVERLAPS *PARTIAL* AND THEY ARE NOT, AND
THAT ONE WORD IS WHAT MADE THE PERMISSIVE READING LOOK FORBIDDEN.** The round-1 review rebuilt wire
provenance from ELK's raw sections and measured the interval relation of every pair: **30 of 30 are
CONTAINMENTS** - one span wholly inside the other, same net, same line, between two **consecutive**
edges of the routed chain (`X:k` and `X:k+1`, meeting at their shared terminal, the second
retracing the first and running on). **0 are partial. 0 are cross-net.** Identical with padding and
the remaining spacings at whole grid steps. Controller ruling **R31** and spec §1.4 revision 5
settle what follows from that; this entry records the defect itself.

`[RAN]` `lib/schgen/elk/graph.ts`'s `edgesForNet` turns a net of degree n into **n-1 two-terminal
edges**, chained - a tree, which is what KiCad draws. **ELK routes each of those edges
independently**, so an edge's route runs back along a stretch an earlier edge of the same net
already occupies. The retrace is the defect; the containment is its measured shape.

**WHAT R31 CHANGED, MEASURED BOTH WAYS.** A same-net collinear containment has exactly one reading -
the interval union *is* the container - so it is collapsed and counted rather than refused. Over all
twelve declared blocks:

| | before R31 | after R31 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| refused at the canonical topology | **11 of 12** | **0 of 12** |
| containments collapsed | n/a (refused) | **30**, 1-6 per block |
| refused at the SNAP gate (**G188**) | 0 | **11 of 12** |
| refused at obligation 3 (**G190**) | 1 | 1 |
| reach the clearance checks | **0** | **0** |

**So R31 removed this entry's barrier entirely and the next one is G188's.** With the G188 probe
spacings as well, the stops are **snap 9, junctions (obligation 2) 2, obligation 3 1** - and those
two junction refusals were this defect's last consequence, and ruling **R33** resolved them (**G199**).

**The per-block canonicalisation, which is G106's figure on this driver:**

| block | duplicates | zero-length | **containments** | wires before -> after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `opamp-buffer/ob-buffer` | 8 | 0 | 5 | 65 -> 52 |
| `optical-compressor/oc-power` | 11 | 0 | 1 | 42 -> 30 |
| `optical-compressor/oc-audio` | 12 | 0 | 5 | 82 -> 65 |
| `optical-compressor/oc-sidechain` | 15 | 0 | 3 | 91 -> 73 |
| `pt2399-core/pt-core` | **24** | 0 | 4 | 179 -> 151 |
| `transistor-preamp/tp-leg-upper` | 0 | 0 | 1 | 14 -> 13 |
| `transistor-preamp/tp-leg-feedback` | 0 | 0 | 1 | 14 -> 13 |
| `transistor-preamp/tp-leg-lower-a` | 0 | 0 | 1 | 14 -> 13 |
| `transistor-preamp/tp-leg-lower-b` | 0 | 0 | 1 | 14 -> 13 |
| `transistor-preamp/tp-leg-collector` | 0 | 0 | 1 | 11 -> 10 |
| `transistor-preamp/tp-leg-emitter-bypass` | 0 | 0 | 1 | 12 -> 11 |
| `transistor-preamp/tp-stage` | 11 | 0 | 6 | 75 -> 58 |

**`oc-sidechain`'s row is new at round 2**: round 1 returned no counts on the obligation-3 arm, so
the one block that takes it was missing from the measurement entirely, along with its 15 duplicates.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 13, Step 6. **Characterised correctly at round 2 by the review**, which
  measured the interval relation this writer had asserted without measuring.
- **Evidence** the census (`tools/schgen/elk/obstacle-census.ts`, run over `PARITY_CASES`) before
  and after R31; the two-arm re-run with the G188 spacings. A check that could have failed:
  `tests/schgen/elk/junctions.test.ts` drives a containment (collapses, counted), a genuine partial
  (refuses, naming *"NEITHER span contains the other"*), a cross-net containment (refuses) and an
  exact duplicate (counted separately) - so the three arms are distinguished by tests rather than by
  this prose, and the partial arm is driven although the corpus never produces one.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED for the census tables and the canonicalisation counts - this writer ran
  them. **RELAYED for the 30/30/0 interval characterisation**, which is the review's measurement;
  this writer confirmed its consequence independently (all 11 clause-(d) refusals clear under R31's
  containment collapse, and the containment count is exactly 30). **RELAYED for the per-algorithm
  table and the star measurement below** - both are the review's probes, and round 2's Verified line
  wrongly claimed *"CONFIRMED for every figure in the tables"* while the prose beside it said whose
  they were. This writer has NOT run `mrtree`, `radial`, `stress` or `force`, nor built a star
  model.
- **Why it is open** the retrace is still there. R31 makes it harmless to the topology and
  **countable**, which is better than refused, but `contained` is now the measure of a backend
  defect rather than a defect that stops the generator.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: a net's route holds no same-net collinear overlap at all -
  every pair of its segments shares at most a point.** That is strictly stronger than what R31 needs
  and is the state a tree-routed net would be in.

  **MECHANISM 1 - one `ElkExtendedEdge` per net - DOES NOT RUN, AND NOBODY MAY FOLLOW IT.** Round 1
  of this entry recommended it as the preferred fix. The review probed it before anyone acted, and
  at the pinned version with the algorithm spec §1.1 requires it raises:

  ```
  java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Passed edge is not 'simple'.
  ```

  for **any** edge carrying more than one source or target - on all twelve blocks **and** on a
  three-node minimal graph. Per algorithm:

  | algorithm | a multi-terminal edge |
  | --- | --- |
  | `layered` (spec §1.1's, and **D4**'s) | **raises** `IllegalArgumentException: Passed edge is not 'simple'.` |
  | `stress`, `force` | **raise** `UnsupportedGraphException: Graph must not contain hyperedges.` |
  | `mrtree`, `radial` | accept it and return **a single section for an n-target edge** - an incomplete route - and neither is an orthogonal router |

  A **star** model (one edge per terminal from a hub) is legal and **worse**: **113 ambiguous pairs
  against 30**. **The edge model is not the lever in either direction.**

  **This is `CLAUDE.md`'s worked example happening again, and the deviation is recorded as the rule
  requires**: round 1's criterion is kept because it was measured; round 1's **mechanism** was
  *"advice from someone who had not yet tried it"* and is withdrawn. **MECHANISM 2**, keeping the
  chain and merging same-net overlaps in the adapter, is what **R31 now does for the containment
  case only** - it was listed at round 1 as forbidden by clause (d), and the ruling is precisely
  that clause (d) never should have covered a containment. **No mechanism is currently offered for
  the residue**, and inventing one here would repeat the fault this paragraph exists to record.

### G190 - `elk.portConstraints = FIXED_POS` does NOT hold a port whose position is off its declared `elk.port.side`, and one real block is caught by it

`[RAN]` `optical-compressor/oc-sidechain`, pin 1 of `D3` (`Device:LED`):

```
node 8382 x 3556     port sent at (762, 1270)     port returned at (0, 1270)
```

The port was sent 762 µm from the node's left edge and came back **on** it. It is not a clamp - the
sent position is inside the node's bounds - it is ELK projecting the port onto the side
`elk.port.side` declares for it, **in spite of `FIXED_POS`**.

**WHY THE PIN IS NOT ON THE EDGE IN THE FIRST PLACE.** A node's size is `u.symbol.boxes.get(u.unit)`
placed, and a symbol's unit box covers its drawn graphics as well as its pins. `Device:LED`'s arrows
extend 762 µm further left than its leftmost pin end, so the pin end sits 762 µm inside the box and
the port is not on the boundary. **Of the 42 ports in that block this is the only one it happens
to**, and across the other eleven blocks it happens to none.

**IT IS CAUGHT, WHICH IS THE POINT.** Spec §1.4 obligation 3 says the transform is applied once
*"and the result is what both ELK and the emitter see"*. `portCoordinateDisagreements` compares the
two and `adaptElkLayout` refuses on a difference, so the block does not draw with a wire attached
762 µm from its pin. **This is the first time that check has had anything to catch**, and it caught
it on real data rather than on a fixture.

**A SECOND FINDING INSIDE THIS ONE: obligation 3's SUBSTITUTION is unobservable whenever FIXED_POS
IS honoured.** `[RAN]` Step 8's perturbation 3 - delete the substitution in `read-graph.ts` and use
ELK's returned section endpoints - **changed no test outcome at all** before a test was written for
it, because the two values agree everywhere the constraint holds. A guard that is invisible exactly
when nothing is wrong is no guard; `tests/schgen/elk/adapt.test.ts` now manufactures the
disagreement in the fixture (one section's start displaced by a grid step) and asserts the wire
still attaches at the recomputed pin end.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 13, Step 6.
- **Evidence** the port dump above, printed from a real `layoutBlocks` run over
  `oc-sidechain`, together with the sweep that found 0 of 42 port offsets outside their node's
  bounds - which is what rules out clamping. For the second half: perturbation 3 run before and
  after the new test, green then red.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer ran both.
- **Why it is open** it is a property of `elkjs`'s port handling at the pinned version, and the fix
  is not the adapter's: the adapter's job is to refuse, and it does.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: every port `elkjs` returns is at the position it was sent
  to, or the block refuses.** The second half is met. For the first, **MECHANISMS, both untried:**
  (1) size a node by the span of its PINS rather than by its symbol box, so every port is on a
  boundary - which changes every node's size and therefore every serialized input, and makes a
  node smaller than the graphics it contains, so bodies could overlap where ELK thinks they do not;
  (2) stop sending `elk.port.side` for a port that is not on a boundary, which gives ELK nothing to
  project onto - and gives up the one mechanism spec §1.2 says transfers from `netlistsvg` for that
  port. Neither is this task's to choose.

### G191 - Step 6's obstacle-pair result is EMPTY, and the reason is that nothing reaches the clearance checks

Spec §1.4 requires the clearance checks to be **re-validated** against ELK geometry, because the
~160 refusals *"were grown against template-produced geometry"* one pair at a time and *"pointing a
pairwise-accreted check set at a new geometry source is exactly the condition that creates a fresh
blind spot."* **G125** records that **95 of the matrix's 105 cells rest on reading the ported source
rather than on a test that could have failed.**

**THE RESULT, AND IT IS A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN AN OMISSION: no `PAIR_COVERAGE` pair fires on ELK
geometry, because 0 of the 12 declared blocks reach `checkLayout` at all.** Eleven refuse at the
canonical topology (**G189**) and one at obligation 3 (**G190**), and the figures are the same with
ELK's remaining spacings at whole grid steps (**G188**). **So the 95 cells have exactly as much
evidence as they had before this task: none.** The re-validation §1.4 asks for has NOT been done, and
reading this entry as "the matrix held up against a second geometry source" would be the
substitution G125 exists to refuse.

**What DID fire, on fixture geometry under the G188 probe arm**, is recorded because it is the only
pair evidence this task produced and because it is a warning about the cells it touches:

```
overlaps | value of power symbol GND 1 at (34.29, 17.78) | label OUT at (39.37, 19.05)
```

- the pair is **`field-text` / `label-outline`**, a cell the matrix records as CHECKED;
- two further blocks produced `"no place for its Reference and Value"`, which
  `problem-obstacles.ts` correctly reports as naming **no pair at all** - a field-placement refusal
  is not a clearance pair, and the census reports it separately rather than inventing one.

**ROUND 5, ON THE LANDED CONFIGURATION: FIVE BLOCKS DRAW, AND EXACTLY ONE PAIR FIRES.** Ruling
**R33**'s split landed, and the probe-arm result below does **not** carry over unchanged - which is
itself the finding, and the reason a probe arm is never reported as a result.

| | R32 probe arm (not landed) | **R33, landed** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **drawn** | 0 | **5 of 12** |
| reach `checkLayout` and fail | 10 | 5 |
| refused earlier | 2 | 2 |
| **pairs fired** | `wire`/`wire` (10 blocks), `body`/`label-outline` (1) | **`body`/`label-outline` only (1 block)** |

**`wire`/`wire` no longer fires, and it was never a second defect.** All 25 of its findings were the
containment collapse's mid-wire ends; R33 splits the segment there, so the end becomes a coincident
end and `checkWireSafety` is silent. **The probe arm was measuring unsplit geometry** - it fired
because mechanism (2) left those ends in place, which is precisely why mechanism (2) was reversed.

**THE LANDED RESULT, in full:**

- **5 blocks draw**: `tp-leg-upper`, `tp-leg-feedback`, `tp-leg-lower-a`, `tp-leg-lower-b`,
  `tp-leg-collector` - the first geometry this generator has ever produced from ELK;
- **5 reach `checkLayout` and are refused**: `ob-buffer`, `oc-power`, `pt-core`,
  `tp-leg-emitter-bypass`, `tp-stage`;
- **2 never reach it**: `oc-audio` at the snap gate (**G196**) and `oc-sidechain` at obligation 3
  (**G190**);
- **one pair fires**: **`body`/`label-outline`**, constraint *overlaps*, on `tp-stage` -
  `body of Q1#1` against `label BYPASS_CAP at (11.43, 11.43)`. The matrix marks that cell
  **`checked`**;
- **five problems name no pair at all** and are reported separately rather than counted as matrix
  evidence: all five are *"no place for its Reference and Value"* field-placement refusals, on
  `ob-buffer`, `oc-power`, `pt-core`, `tp-leg-emitter-bypass` and `tp-stage`.

**AND THE CAVEAT IS LOUDER THAN THE RESULT. 12 of the 14 obstacle categories never appear**
(`body` and `label-outline` are the two that do, through the single pair that fired):
`pin-line`, `pin-number`, `pin-name`, `interior-graphic`, `wire`, `junction`, `power-glyph`,
`pwr-flag-glyph`, `field-text`, `frame-border`, `no-connect-marker` and `dnp-cross` are untouched -
**twelve names, which is what the count must say.** **This is evidence for 1 cell of 105.** §1.4 predicts *"a fresh blind spot"* from pointing a pairwise-accreted check set at a
new geometry source, and **no uncovered and no reason-only cell fired** - but **an absent blind spot
on geometry this narrow is not an absent blind spot.** Five blocks of one circuit family drew; the
other three circuits produced nothing that reached the matrix at all.

**ROUND 4: TWO PAIRS FIRE. THIS IS THE FIRST EVIDENCE ANY OF G125's 95 UNEVIDENCED CELLS HAS EVER
HAD, AND THE FIRST READING WAS TAKEN UNDER A PROBE ARM** (ruling
R32's mechanism (2), which is NOT landed). With the emitter's junctions sourced from
`branchJunctions`, **10 of 12 blocks reach `checkLayout`** - from 0 - and:

| pair | matrix says | constraint | blocks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **`wire` / `wire`** | **checked** | *wire end mid-wire* | **10** |
| **`body` / `label-outline`** | **checked** | *overlaps* | 1 (`tp-stage`) |

```
wire|wire            e.g. wire 3 of ob-buffer || wire 4 of ob-buffer at (41.91, 29.21)
body|label-outline   e.g. body of Q1#1 || label BYPASS_CAP at (11.43, 11.43)
```

**BOTH CELLS WERE ALREADY MARKED `checked` IN THE MATRIX, AND THAT IS THE RESULT RATHER THAN A
DISAPPOINTMENT.** §1.4's re-validation clause predicts *"a fresh blind spot"* from pointing a
pairwise-accreted check set at a new geometry source; **on this geometry no uncovered or
reason-only cell fired at all.** What fired is two cells the matrix already claims, so the
prediction is **not** borne out here - which is a finding about the matrix's accreted set holding
up on a second source, and it is the first time that claim has had any evidence either way.

ELK's.**

### G193 - an anchor's SIDE is taken from the reviewed rule and not from ELK's route, and the two disagree on 18 of the 38 boundary anchors

`Anchor.side` is read by `anchorsToSymbols`, which turns it into a power symbol's ROTATION through
`powerRotation` - so it decides which way a `GND` or `+9V` glyph points.

The first version of `lib/schgen/elk/read-graph.ts` derived it from the direction ELK's route
arrives from, on the reasoning that a glyph should line up with its own wire. **That overrules a
convention stated in the tree**: `RailSpec` in `lib/schgen/ir/types.ts` says *"Ground rails are
drawn at the bottom of blocks with downward symbols; supplies at the top"*, and
`lib/schgen/authoring.ts`'s `negotiablePort` is the reviewed rule that applies it. A derivation
invented in an adapter may not displace a stated rule - `CLAUDE.md`'s *"a stated directive
outranks"*, pointed at a rule file rather than at a board.

**IT IS NOT A COSMETIC DIFFERENCE. Measured over all twelve ELK-selecting blocks, 38 boundary
anchors:**

| | anchors |
| --- | --- |
| the reviewed rule gives ONE side and it AGREES with the route | 4 |
| the reviewed rule gives ONE side and it DISAGREES | **18** |
| the reviewed rule leaves the side open (`bidirectional`, or no declared direction) | 16 |

Every one of the 18 is a rail whose declaration says `up` or `down` and whose route arrives
horizontally - `ob-buffer`'s `GND` (declared down, route right), its `VCC` and `VEE` (declared up,
route right), and so on. Under `elk.direction = RIGHT` a boundary node is placed in a LAYER, so a
rail is almost always reached sideways, and the route-derived rule would have rotated 18 of 22
decided glyphs 90 degrees off the convention.

**The route still decides the 16 the rule leaves open**, because choosing between left and right by
taste is what this layer must not do, and the direction the wire actually arrives from is ELK's
geometry rather than anyone's preference. That residue is **G99**'s *"settled at the circuit
boundary, OPEN below it"* reaching the drawing.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 13, Step 7. **The evidence that prompted the change was WRONG and the
  reasoning that settled it was not**, which is worth recording: the drawing that showed a `+3V3`
  arrow pointing downwards was `rail-row`'s and not ELK's (**G192**). The change stands on the
  stated convention and on the 18/38 measurement, both of which are independent of that picture.
- **Evidence** the 38-anchor sweep above, run over every ELK-selecting block of the four parity
  circuits, comparing `negotiablePort`'s answer against the route-derived one per anchor.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer ran the sweep and made the change.
- **Why it is open** the 16 anchors the rule leaves open are decided by geometry, and nothing has
  reviewed whether that is the right answer for them; it is recorded rather than defended.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: an anchor's side comes from a reviewed rule wherever one
  has an answer, and from stated geometry where none does - never from a preference expressed in the
  adapter.** Met as far as `negotiablePort` reaches. **MECHANISM for the residue, untried:** declare
  a direction for the nets that cross a BLOCK boundary without being a port of the network, which is
  G99's open fifth input and is a declaration question rather than a geometry one.

### G195 - spec §1.4 obligation 3 says "rotation AND mirroring", and mirroring is unrepresentable anywhere in this generator

`[CODE]` `Rotation` in `lib/schgen/render/geometry.ts` is `0 | 90 | 180 | 270` and **nothing else**.
`grep -rn "mirror" --include="*.ts" lib/` returns **8 lines and not one is geometric**: a netlist
writer's *"the mirror of importLegacyNetlist"*, a validator *"mirroring"* another module's shape,
and six SPICE-model provenance notes about download mirrors. There is no mirror axis on `Placement`,
no mirror in `pinEnd`, `placeBox` or `rotate`, and no KiCad `(mirror x)` in the emitter.

**So obligation 3's second verb cannot be checked, and until now nothing said so.** The obligation
reads *"Port positions survive rotation **and mirroring** by being recomputed, never carried"*, and
§1.5 states the semantic half it protects: *"the same NPN mirrored for readability keeps its pin
identity - mirroring moves geometry, never pin assignment. A transform that changes which terminal a
pad or wire reaches is a defect, not a style."* **Half of that sentence is about an operation this
generator cannot perform.**

**IT IS NOT A HOLE IN THE CHECK, IT IS A HOLE IN THE VOCABULARY**, and the distinction matters for
whoever closes it. Task 13's four-link test exercises the obligation as far as the model reaches: a
five-pin `Fix:REG3` at rotation 0 and at 180, every pin keeping its net while the geometry moves on
both axes. **A rotation by 180 is not a mirror** - it preserves handedness, and a reflection does
not - so no test in this repository has ever exercised a transform that could swap a pin's identity
by reflection, because no such transform exists to exercise.

- **Found** 2026-10-20 by the Task 13 round-1 review, recorded at round 2.
- **Evidence** the `Rotation` declaration read directly; the `grep` above with all 8 hits
  classified; and `tests/schgen/elk/adapt.test.ts`'s rotation test, which covers rotation only. A
  check that could have failed: KiCad's symbol instances carry a `(mirror x|y)` token and the
  emitter writes none, so a round-trip of a mirrored symbol would not survive - nothing exercises
  that because nothing produces one.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer ran the grep and read the type. **RELAYED for the finding
  itself**, which is the review's.
- **Why it is open** adding a mirror is a change to `Placement`, to `pinEnd`/`placeBox`, to the
  emitter and to every clearance check that reads a placed box - and **nothing in the tree wants one
  yet**, because §1.5's authority order gives orientations to templates and to a rule library that
  returns rotations. It is recorded so that nobody reads obligation 3 as fully discharged.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: either a mirrored placement is representable and the
  four-link test covers one, or spec §1.4 obligation 3 is amended to say that mirroring is out of
  scope at this milestone.** **The second is a controller decision and is probably the right one for
  M1**; it is named first because it is cheaper and because an obligation nothing can satisfy is
  worse than an obligation deliberately narrowed. **MECHANISM for the first, untried:** add a
  `mirror: "none" | "x" | "y"` to `Placement`, thread it through `rotate`/`pinEnd`/`placeBox`, and
  emit KiCad's `(mirror …)`. The cost is every consumer of a placed box, which is most of
  `lib/schgen/render/`.

### G196 - obligation 1's MEMBERSHIP arm had never run on any real block, and the first time it ran it fired

Spec §1.4 obligation 1 requires **two** sets to be unchanged by snapping: *"the set of distinct wire
geometries and the set of net memberships."* `snapToGrid` computes both. **Until round 3 the second
had never been evaluated on a single block of the four parity circuits, and nothing said so.**

**WHY IT COULD NOT RUN, which is structural rather than incidental.** `snapToGrid` computes the
partition only when the first two arms are clean:

```ts
if (collapsed.length === 0) { const was = partition(...); const now = partition(...) }
```

That gate is not arbitrary - `connectedComponents` calls `assertWireShape`, which **throws** on a
zero-length wire, so the membership comparison cannot be attempted on geometry the zero-length arm
has already condemned. And **G188**'s 10 µm jogs meant the zero-length arm fired on every block. So
arm 3 was unreachable on the whole corpus, by construction, and a reader of the 3363-pass suite had
nothing to tell them.

**WITH G188's OPTIONS SET, IT RUNS - AND IT FIRES ON ONE BLOCK.** `[RAN]` Over all twelve:

| arm | findings |
| --- | --- |
| zero-length | **0** |
| geometry merge | **0** |
| **membership** | **1** - `optical-compressor/oc-audio` |

```
snapping changed which nets the geometry joins: 15 connected piece(s) became 14
pieces lost: OUT_PRE
```

**The merge is SAME-NET**: two separate pieces of `OUT_PRE` became one. No component's net set
gained a net, so nothing is shorted - but the partition changed, which is exactly what the
obligation says must not happen, and the gate refuses. **Whether a same-net piece merge should
refuse at all is a real question this entry does not answer.** Two pieces of one net joining is
electrically harmless and arguably what the drawing wanted; the obligation as written does not
distinguish it from a cross-net merge, and neither does the gate.

**THE ROUND-2 REVIEW's FIGURES FOR THIS ARM WERE TAKEN BEFORE THE OPTIONS CHANGED AND ARE RECORDED
AS SUCH.** On the pre-round-3 options it measured **265 cross-net endpoint pairs** distinct before
snapping and coincident after, across 6 blocks (`pt-core` 197, `tp-stage` 25, `ob-buffer` 18,
`oc-audio` 14, `oc-sidechain` 9, `tp-leg-emitter-bypass` 2) with separations up to **585.92 µm**,
and **18 of 20 merge findings genuine and ALL cross-net** - `GND`+`VCC`, `GND`+`OUT_PRE`,
`BASE`+`OUT`, `INPUT`+`Net-(C7-Pad1)` - at 10-31 µm closest approach. **Coalescing those would have
shorted the circuit, and the gate was right about every one.** `[RAN]` **On the round-3 options all
of those are gone**: 0 cross-net endpoint pairs, 0 geometry merges. They were a consequence of the
sub-grid jogs, not of the routing.

**AND ONE ANALYTIC POINT THAT CORRECTS HOW THIS WAS FRAMED.** A merge requires BOTH coordinates to
fall in one rounding bucket, so **no merged pair can be a grid step or more apart on either axis** -
the sub-grid-versus-grid split cannot discriminate a benign merge from a dangerous one. **The split
that does is same-net versus cross-net**, and that is the distinction any future refinement of
obligation 1 has to be built on.

**ROUND 5: `oc-audio` IS NOT THE LAST BLOCK STANDING, AND THE DECISION IS STILL THE CONTROLLER'S.**
Ruling **R33** made 5 of 12 blocks draw. `oc-audio` still refuses here, on the same same-net
`OUT_PRE` piece merge - but it is **one of seven blocks that do not draw**, and one of **two** that
never reach the clearance checks (the other is `oc-sidechain`, at obligation 3, **G190**). The other
five reach `checkLayout` and are refused by it.

**So the question this entry raises is not yet on the critical path**, and it is recorded rather
than decided: whether obligation 1's membership arm should refuse a merge that joins two pieces of
ONE net - which shorts nothing and which the drawing arguably wanted - is a change to what the
obligation means, and that is not this task's to make. If a later change makes the other six draw,
`oc-audio` becomes the last one standing and the question becomes urgent.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 13 round 3, after **G188**'s options unmasked the arm.
- **Evidence** the three-arm count over all twelve blocks, run here; `oc-audio`'s refusal text
  verbatim; the gate's own `if (collapsed.length === 0)` read directly, and `assertWireShape`'s
  throw in `connectivity.ts` which is why the gate is there. **A check that could have failed:**
  `tests/schgen/elk/snap.test.ts`'s *"snapping that changes a net's membership REFUSES"* drives the
  arm on a hand-built fixture and has passed throughout - so the arm was correct all along and only
  unreachable on real geometry, which is the distinction this entry exists to draw.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED for the round-3 figures and for the structural account - this writer ran
  and read them. **RELAYED for the 265 pairs and the 18 cross-net merges**, which are the round-2
  review's measurements on the pre-round-3 options; this writer confirmed only that both are zero
  now.
- **Why it is open** `oc-audio` still refuses, and whether a same-net piece merge ought to is
  unsettled. It is also a standing hazard: a gate arm can be live and structurally invisible, and
  a passing suite says nothing about which arms ran.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: every arm of every gate in the realization contract is
  known to have been evaluated on real geometry, or is recorded as unreachable with the reason.**
  This entry discharges that for obligation 1's three arms; **no equivalent audit has been done for
  obligations 2 to 5**. **MECHANISM, untried:** have `snapToGrid` report which arms it evaluated
  rather than only what they found, so the census can print arm coverage beside its results - which
  makes an unreachable arm visible without anybody thinking to look for one.

### G197 - R32's gate FIRED: the crystal template's junction set changes, and the cause is that the two rules count a coincident PIN differently

Ruling **R32** gates mechanism (2) - sourcing the emitter's junctions from `branchJunctions` rather
than `junctionPoints` - on a measurement: *"compute both junction sets for every template-drawn
block and every ELK block, and report the difference… If any template sheet changes, STOP and
report it."*

`[RAN]` **Nine template-drawn blocks examined** - the `mini` design's seven wired blocks, covering
`regulator`, `decoupling-bank`, `divider`, `connector-fanout` (twice), `opamp-stage` and `crystal`,
plus `rail-row` and `passive-chain` fixtures for the two the design does not use. **Eight agree
exactly. One differs**, and it is `mini/XTAL`, the `crystal` template, at a single point:

```
TEMPLATE(crystal) mini/XTAL: junctionPoints=3 branchJunctions=2
                             onlyPoints=[(0, 5.08)]  onlyBranch=[]
```

**THE CAUSE, DIAGNOSED RATHER THAN RECONCILED.** At `(0, 5.08)` there are **three items: one `GND`
wire end, and TWO pins of `Y1` - pins 2 and 4, both on `GND`, both at that point.**

- **`junctionPoints` counts pin ends individually**: 1 + 2 = 3, which meets its *"3 or more wire
  ends and pin ends coincide"* rule, so it emits a dot;
- **`branchJunctions` counts "a pin is here" as a BOOLEAN**: `atPin ? 1 : 0`, so 1 + 1 = 2, which is
  below its branch threshold and it emits nothing.

**NEITHER RULE IS ELECTRICALLY WRONG, AND THAT IS THE FINDING.** In KiCad a wire end coincident with
pins connects to them natively; a junction there is **neither required nor harmful**. So the
difference is **one cosmetic dot on one template sheet**, not a connection gained or lost. Sheet
level corroborates the per-block measurement: the `signal` sheet goes from **5 junctions to 4** (the
XTAL dot) and the `power` sheet is **unchanged at 7**.

**IT IS RECORDED AND NOT FIXED.** R32 says *"do not reconcile it by adjusting either rule until the
difference has been read"*, and reading it is what this entry is. **It is also now moot for the
decision it was gating** - see **G199**: mechanism (2) could not make anything draw, so the question of
whether to accept one lost dot on the crystal sheet does not arise until that is settled.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 13 round 4, running R32's gate before landing anything.
- **Evidence** the nine-block comparison above; the item dump at `(0, 5.08)` naming `Y1.2` and
  `Y1.4`; `branchesOf`'s `atPin ? 1 : 0` read directly in `lib/schgen/elk/junctions.ts`;
  `junctionPoints`' *"3 or more wire ends and pin ends"* read in `render/connectivity.ts`; and the
  sheet-level counts for both `mini` sheets. A check that could have failed: eight of the nine
  template blocks agreed exactly, so the comparison is not reporting a difference everywhere.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer ran every measurement.
- **Why it is open** nothing is changed. If a later ruling takes mechanism (2), this must be settled
  first; if it takes mechanism (1), `branchJunctions` never becomes the emitter's source and the
  difference stays a curiosity about two rules that are each right for their own job.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: the two rules agree on every template-drawn block, or the
  one that is wrong for its stated purpose is identified and fixed.** **MECHANISM, untried and NOT
  taken:** make `branchJunctions` count coincident pins rather than testing for any - `ends + 2 *
  through + pinCount`. That is a one-line change and it would make the sets agree on `XTAL`, but
  **it is a change to what counts as a branch**, and whether two coincident pins of one part on one
  net constitute a current division is a question nobody here has answered. It is not taken on the
  authority of making two numbers match.


### G199 - a PARTITION comparison cannot answer a JUNCTION question, and a gate built on one will refuse what the schematic would have connected

**THIS ENTRY CARRIES FORWARD WHAT G194 AND G198 ESTABLISHED. Both are deleted**: their defect -
the containment collapse leaving a branch with no junction - is resolved by ruling **R33**, which
splits the container so the join is by coincident ends and needs no junction at all. What is NOT
resolved is the reusable hazard underneath them, and it is recorded here so the next gate does not
hit it.

**THE HAZARD.** `lib/schgen/render/connectivity.ts` joins a wire to another wire or to a pin **only
at coincident ENDS**, and says why in its own module comment: *"a pin end or wire end on a wire's
INTERIOR connects ONLY with a junction there"*, and *"the generator never relies on the
junction-dependent cases … junction dots are cosmetic."* **So `connectedComponents` is junction-blind
by construction.** Any check that compares two connectivity partitions through it is therefore
answering *"what connects without junctions"*, which is a different question from *"what the
schematic will connect"* whenever a junction is in play.

**IT WAS HIT, AND THE COST IS MEASURED.** Task 13 round 2 wrote a guard asserting that R31's
containment collapse preserves the partition. `[RAN]` **It fires on 12 of 12 blocks** - on
`tp-leg-upper` a 4-piece partition becomes 5 - and with it in place **R31 could not take effect on a
single block**. The collapse was correct; the guard was asking a junction question with a model that
excludes junctions. It was deleted, and the gate that genuinely sees the case is spec §1.4
obligation 2, which compares required branch points against emitted junctions.

**AND THE SAME BLINDNESS, READ FROM THE OTHER SIDE, IS WHAT REVERSED A RULING.** `[RAN]` Ruling
**R32** took the mechanism of emitting a junction at every required branch point. It satisfied
obligation 2 and was then refused by `checkWireSafety` **at the same 25 points and at 0 others** -
one collapsed containment, one branch point, one junction emitted, one refusal - because that
check embodies the *"split the wire there"* policy rather than the junction-dependent one.
**Mechanism (2) would have built connectivity on dots this generator's own policy calls cosmetic.**
Ruling **R33** reverses it; the full reasoning is in spec §1.4 and is not duplicated here.

**WHAT A LATER READER SHOULD TAKE FROM THIS.** Before building a check on `connectedComponents`,
ask whether the question involves a junction. If it does, that function cannot answer it, and the
check will be confidently wrong in the direction of **refusing geometry the schematic would have
connected** - the expensive direction, because it stops a drawing rather than shipping a bad one.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 13 rounds 2 and 4; consolidated at round 5 when R33 resolved the two
  entries it is drawn from.
- **Evidence** the 4-to-5 partition measurement on `tp-leg-upper`, printed by the guard before it
  was removed; the 25/25 classification of `checkWireSafety`'s *"mid-wire"* findings against the
  collapse's branch points, with `elsewhere` separately reported and equal to 0;
  `connectivity.ts`'s module comment read directly. A check that could have failed and now stands:
  `tests/schgen/elk/junctions.test.ts`'s *"after the split, junctionPoints and branchJunctions
  agree and wire-safety is silent"* asserts all three agree on split geometry **and** that the
  UNSPLIT geometry is what wire-safety refuses, so neither half can pass by finding nothing.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer ran every measurement and wrote and deleted the guard.
- **WHAT NOW COVERS G194's CRITERION, which the deletion would otherwise have left unanswered.**
  That entry asked that *"every point that carries a join in the pre-collapse topology still carries
  one in the emitted schematic."* On the final geometry it is `checkLayout` that answers:
  **`componentProblems`** reports any piece of a labelled net with no label or power symbol and any
  short between two nets, and **`internalSplitProblems`** reports an internal net split into more
  than one piece - both over `connectedComponents` of the layout being returned. `[RAN]` **All five
  drawn blocks pass both with zero problems**, so the join survives the collapse-and-split in the
  geometry that is actually emitted, checked by code rather than by argument.
- **Why it is open** it is a property of a ported module that this repository relies on and does not
  intend to change, and it is a trap any future gate can fall into. It is not a defect to fix.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: no check in the realization contract compares connectivity
  through `connectedComponents` to answer a question whose answer depends on a junction.** Met
  today: obligation 1's membership arm compares partitions and is about coincident ends only, and
  obligation 2 compares junction SETS rather than partitions. **MECHANISM, untried:** state the
  limit on `connectedComponents` itself rather than in its module header, so a caller sees it at
  the call site - which is where the guard that had to be deleted was written.

### G200 - the first evidence for spec §1.7's "one visual language": ELK draws a STAIRCASE where a template draws a column, and 47% of nets double back

**Step 7 is done.** A block that **selects** the ELK backend and **draws** was emitted through the
real `generate`, exported with `kicad-cli` and read. Until round 6 it could not be: `elkBackendFrom`
threw a refusal naming `adaptElkLayout` as *"not written yet"* when it had existed since round 1,
and a test pinned the throw (**G201**).

**WHAT IS RIGHT, AND IT IS THE part R31 AND R33 ARE ABOUT.** **Junctions sit exactly at the branch
points and nowhere else.** The emitted sheet carries three, each at a degree-3 node - the `3V3` rail
where two resistors and the rail anchor meet, the collector node where two resistors and the
transistor meet, and the ground node. **That is R33 working, visible in ink**: before it, those were
a wire end lying on another wire's interior, which KiCad does not join.

**WHAT IS WRONG IS THE SHAPE, AND IT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN DESCRIBED.** Over the five blocks that
draw:

| | measured |
| --- | --- |
| placements | 14 |
| **distinct x-coordinates** | **14** |
| **parts sharing an x-coordinate** | **0** |
| nets | 19 |
| segments | 67 (**3.53 per net**) |
| total wire | 224.0 grid steps |
| **nets whose route REVERSES direction on an axis** | **9 of 19 (47%)** |

**THE STAIRCASE.** **No two parts share an x-coordinate - 14 of 14.** Every block is a diagonal
cascade: a horizontal run, down through a part, a step right, down through the next. A
template-drawn `divider` of the same topology is a **vertical column**, with its two parts on one x.
**So an ELK block beside a template block does not look like the same hand drew it**, which is
exactly what §1.7's *"one visual language"* requires and this is the first evidence anyone has had
about it either way.

**THE DOUBLING-BACK.** **47% of nets reverse direction on an axis**: the route leaves a pin, runs
away from its destination, turns, and comes back past where it started. On the emitted sheet the
transistor's base leaves leftward, rises, and runs right again *over the top of the part* to reach a
resistor that sits above and to the right - **three segments where one would do.** It is systematic
rather than incidental, and its shape points at port side assignment rather than at bad luck: the
base pin is on the symbol's left, so the route must leave leftward whatever is to the right of it.

**NEITHER IS THIS ADAPTER's TO FIX, AND NEITHER IS FIXED.** Both are properties of
`lib/schgen/elk/graph.ts` - the per-net spanning-chain edge model (**G189**) and the port sides it
fixes from the symbol's own geometry. `CLAUDE.md` says driving a measurable cost down is work to
automate rather than hand back, and **that is why these are measured here**: segment count, total
length and reversal rate are numbers a later task can drive down and be held to.

**ONE CAVEAT THAT IS NOT AN ELK FINDING.** The emitted sheet is roughly 85% empty, with the block in
the top-left corner. That is `packFrames` and its block exclusion, not the router.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 13 round 6, performing Step 7 for the first time.
- **Evidence** the emitted `.kicad_sch`, its PDF and the rendered PNG, read directly; `generate`
  reporting `ELK pre-pass outcomes: 1 ELKBLK=laid out` and the sheet carrying 17 wires, 3 junctions
  and 4 symbols; and the table above, computed over the five parity blocks that draw. A check that
  could have failed: the staircase measure compares placement count against distinct x-count, so a
  single shared x would show as a non-zero difference, and the reversal measure reports the
  denominator.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer emitted, rendered and read the sheet and ran the
  measurements. **The qualitative reading matches the round-5 review's independent description of
  `tp-leg-upper`**, which reached a picture through a hand-written `Backend`.
- **Why it is open** nothing here is fixed. The shape is a property of the edge model, and the edge
  model's one proposed change does not run at the pinned version (**G189**).
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: an ELK-drawn block and a template-drawn block of the same
  topology read as the same visual language - which for a series pair means a shared axis rather
  than a diagonal - and no net's route reverses direction without a reason in the topology.**
  **MECHANISMS, untried:** none is offered. The obvious ones are layout options, and
  `lib/schgen/elk/options.ts` forbids choosing a value because a drawing improves; a reviewed source
  for a value would have to come first. **The numbers above are the baseline any attempt is measured
  against.**

### G201 - `elkBackendFrom` refused every laid-out block by naming a module that had existed for five rounds, and a test held the statement in place

`[CODE]` `tools/schgen/elk/layout.ts`'s `elkBackendFrom` threw, for the **laid out** outcome:

> *"turning that ElkNode into a BlockLayout is lib/schgen/elk/adapt.ts's adaptElkLayout (Task 13 of
> the M1 schematic-authoring plan), **which is not written yet**."*

**It was written, exported and tested from Task 13 round 1, with exactly `Backend.realise`'s
signature.** The consequence was not cosmetic: `tools/schgen/generate.ts` takes this backend, so
**the real pipeline could not emit a single ELK block for five rounds** - which is why Step 7 went
undone in the round where it first became possible, and why the round-5 review had to write its own
three-line `Backend` to reach a picture.

**AND THE SUITE HELD IT THERE.** `tests/schgen/elk/layout.elk.test.ts` asserted
`toThrow(/adaptElkLayout/)`, so the one check that would have caught the stale refusal was asserting
it. **That is `CLAUDE.md`'s *supersede means delete* and *refusals teach* inverted at once**: a
refusal that names a missing module which is not missing teaches a reader something false, and a
test that pins it makes the falsehood load-bearing.

**FIXED IN ROUND 6**: one line in the backend, and the test now asserts the backend **adapts** -
same verdict and same shape as calling `adaptElkLayout` directly, and explicitly `not.toThrow()`.

- **Found** 2026-10-20 by the Task 13 round-5 review; fixed and recorded at round 6.
- **Evidence** the throw read in the tree at `d7db171`; `generate.ts:159` taking that backend; the
  replaced assertion; and `generate` now reporting `ELK pre-pass outcomes: 1 ELKBLK=laid out` and
  writing a sheet (**G200**).
- **Verified** CONFIRMED for the fix and the emission - this writer made both and read the output.
  **RELAYED for the discovery.**
- **Why it is open** it is recorded rather than open: the defect is fixed. It stays because the
  SHAPE of it is worth a later reader's attention - **a stale refusal with a test pinning it is
  invisible to a green suite**, and this repository has now produced one.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: no refusal in the tree names a module, a task or a state
  that no longer applies.** **MECHANISM, untried:** nothing automatic is proposed - a grep for *"not
  written yet"* and *"does not exist"* across refusal strings would find this class, and is offered
  as a one-off sweep rather than a guard, because a guard over prose is the shape **G125** warns
  about.

### G202 - two statements this task made about its own guards were false, and both were measured false rather than argued away

Recorded together because they are one failure mode - **asserting what a guard does instead of
running it** - and because the register's own rule is that a mechanism is advice from someone who
had not yet tried it.

**(1) THE FOREIGN-NET SPLIT: the stated reason was wrong and the guard is right for a better one.**
Round 5 justified `splitAtBranches` skipping a foreign-net pin by saying a split *"would leave the
geometry unchanged and the defect unreported."* `[RAN]`:

```
UNSPLIT  : ["wire 0 (net A) passes over pin end R_B.1 (B) at (3.81, 0)"]
SPLIT FOR: ["wire 0a (net A) passes over pin end R_B.1 (B) at (3.81, 0)",
            "wire 0b (net A) passes over pin end R_B.1 (B) at (3.81, 0)"]
```

**The defect is still reported - twice.** `wireOverPins`' first clause tests `onSegment`, which
includes endpoints, not `strictlyInside`. **The real reason the guard is right is stronger than the
one given**: a split asserts a branch point on THIS net, and net `A` has no branch where net `B`
happens to have a pin. That is inventing topology, which is precisely what criterion (b) -
*represent each net's branches explicitly* - must not be used to do. The comment in
`lib/schgen/elk/junctions.ts`, the test's doc comment and the report all now say this.

**(2) THE POST-SNAP COUNTS WERE COMPUTED AND DISCARDED, WHILE A COMMENT SAID THEY WERE REPORTED.**
`adaptElkLayout` canonicalises twice - once before snapping and once after. Round 5 returned the
**pre-snap** counts only, derived `wiresAfter` arithmetically from them, and carried a comment
saying the post-snap `contained` and `split` were *"reported in the counts rather than refused."*
They were dropped. Worse, because `wiresAfter` was a derivation rather than a measurement, **a
post-snap split would have made the reported before→after disagree with the geometry actually drawn
and the census's self-consistency assertion would still have passed**, since it checks that
arithmetic against itself. That is exactly the silent count ruling **R33** says must not exist.

**Fixed**: `countsOf` sums both passes, `wiresAfter` is the measured length of the final wire list,
and `adaptElkLayout` **throws** when the counts' own arithmetic disagrees with the wire list it is
about to return - a check nothing in the tree previously performed. Today the two passes agree on
all five drawn blocks (14/14/14/14/11), so this was latent.

**AND THE FIRST VERSION OF THAT CHECK COULD NOT FAIL, WHICH IS THE SAME FAULT ONE LEVEL DOWN.** It
compared `bothPasses.wiresAfter` against `layout.wires.length` - and `wiresAfter` **is**
`layout.wires.length`, passed in two lines above, so it was `x !== x`. **Perturbation 14 deleted the
entire block and nothing went red**, which is how it was caught; the sweep found a tautology that
had been written to guard against a silent count. It now compares the arithmetic - `before` less the
three merges plus the splits - against the returned list, and perturbation 14 turns
`tests/schgen/elk/adapt.test.ts`'s *"the canonicalisation counts add up to the layout that is
returned"* red. That test uses `regulatorBlock` and not the divider for a measured reason: the
grid-aligned divider's four counts are all **zero**, so its arithmetic is `7 - 0 + 0 = 7` and the
assertion would pass without exercising anything.

- **Found** 2026-10-20 by the Task 13 round-5 review; both reproduced and fixed at round 6.
- **Evidence** the two-arm `checkWireSafety` output above, run here; the `counts` construction read
  in `adapt.ts` at `d7db171`; and the new equality throw, which is a check that can fail.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer reproduced both and made both fixes. **RELAYED for the
  discovery of each.**
- **Why it is open** it is recorded rather than open; both are fixed. It stays because the shape is
  worth the next writer's attention: **a justification written beside a guard is a claim, and this
  task shipped two that were false while the guards themselves were right.** A wrong reason attached
  to a right behaviour survives review more easily than a wrong behaviour, and it is what a later
  reader will reason from.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: every justification a guard carries is one the writer has
  run, not one they expect.** **MECHANISM, untried:** state the measurement in the comment, as the
  two above now do - a comment that quotes its own `[RAN]` output cannot drift from the code without
  the output being wrong too.

### G203 - spec §5.2's cross-sheet mechanism is DECIDED: one per CLASS, two classes, two mechanisms - with the reading it rests on, so a later reader can dispute it

Spec revision 4 names *"the M1 plan's Task 15"* as this question's owner and contributes the rule
and the test but not the choice. The choice is below, and the reading it rests on is stated first
because the reading is the disputable part.

**THE READING.** §1.6's original sentence is *"exactly one mechanism carries cross-sheet
connectivity"*, which reads as a demand for uniformity. Revision 4's finding 16 replaces it with
the review's rule, **adopted and quoted**: ***"each CLASS of connection has one authoritative
mechanism, with no ambiguous or duplicate representation."*** Power symbols, global labels and
hierarchical ports *"have different KiCad semantics and may legitimately serve different classes"*.
**So "exactly one" is read as one per class, not one per sheet**, and that is the whole of what
plan decision D5 means here.

**THE DECISION**, in `lib/schgen/render/cross-sheet.ts`:

| class | what states it | mechanism | why that one |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `declared-rail` | `Circuit.rails`, a `RailSpec` in the authoring file | `power-symbol` | spec §3.4's third objective criterion - *"rails must be declared ports, so a rail drawn as an ordinary net is detectable"* |
| `inter-block-signal` | everything else that crosses a boundary | `global-label` | the one remaining mechanism the emitter has, and the only one carrying KiCad's intersheet page references |

**HIERARCHICAL PORTS ARE EMITTED BY NOTHING, AND THAT IS A DECISION.** `anchorsToSymbols` in
`lib/schgen/render/power-text.ts` emits exactly two things for a block's boundary anchors, and
`emit.ts` writes exactly those. A third class needing a third mechanism is a change to this
decision with its own reasoning and its own round-trip case.

**`crossSheetProblems` HAS FIVE CLAUSES AND THE TASK 15 BRIEF NAMES THREE.** The brief's three are
a net drawn with both mechanisms, a net crossing a boundary with neither, and a class with no
stated mechanism. The two added:

- **a class stated to use a mechanism the emitter cannot draw** (`unemittableMechanisms`). This is
  what Step 7's first perturbation drives, and it is separate from the unmapped-class clause
  because the two failures are different sentences;
- **a net drawn with a mechanism other than the one its class states.** Without it `classOf` and
  `mechanismFor` are read by nobody: **a rail drawn only as a global label passes all three of the
  brief's clauses**, and spec §3.4's third criterion is exactly that case.

**ROUND 2: THE CROSSING-WITH-NEITHER CLAUSE WAS PER-SET AND IS NOW PER-SHEET, and the difference
is the whole usefulness of it.** `drawnWith` unions a net's representation over every drawing, so
the clause asked *"is this net drawn ANYWHERE"* and fired only when the answer was nowhere.
`[RAN]` on the three-sheet `SIG` fixture through the real `generate`: stripping s3's label alone
reported **nothing**; stripping s2's and s3's reported **nothing**; only stripping all three
fired. **The likely instance - one sheet's piece left unrepresented and electrically orphaned
while the other sheets carry the net - was invisible.** The clause now asks it of every sheet
carrying a pin of the net and names the sheet, and the three cases above report 1, 2 and 3.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 15, Steps 1-3; the per-sheet correction at round 2, by the review.
- **Evidence** `tests/schgen/render/cross-sheet.kicad.test.ts`, which drives each clause over real
  generated drawings. Checks that could have failed: a rail's power symbols replaced by global
  labels reports *"net GND is a \"declared-rail\" connection, whose one authoritative mechanism is
  \"power-symbol\", and it is drawn with \"global-label\""*; the unperturbed drawings report
  nothing. `unmappedClasses` is driven with a table missing an entry and with the shipped table,
  and only the first reports.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED for the decision and for the per-sheet fix - this writer wrote the
  module and the tests and ran them. **RELAYED for the discovery of the per-set weakness**,
  which is the round-2 review's, driven here before it was changed.
- **Why it is open** it is a DECISION recorded so it can be disputed, not a defect. The reading
  above is the arguable part: a reader who thinks §1.6 meant one mechanism per SHEET would refuse
  this design, and the spec's revision-4 note is the evidence that it does not.
- **What would settle it** nothing - it is settled unless the owner reverses it. **A caution:** the
  round trip (below) establishes that the COMBINATION behaves; it does not establish that either
  mechanism is the best one for its class, and no measurement here compares them.

### G204 - spec §1.6's one-sheet-against-many net-membership test, RUN: three cases, three agreements, and one fixture rewritten because the first version could not have failed

The test is the spec reviewer's, adopted as written: *"generate the same network as one sheet and
as multiple sheets, export both through `kicad-cli`, and verify identical net membership."*

**THE THREE PARTITIONS, SIDE BY SIDE.** `[RAN]` Each fixture in
`tests/schgen/__fixtures__/designs/crosssheet.ts` is generated twice - every block on one A1 sheet,
and the declared assignment across A3 sheets - written, and exported with
`kicad-cli sch export netlist --format kicadsexpr`.

| case | sheets | one sheet | many sheets |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **shared rail** | 2 | `GND:[R1.2,R2.2,R3.2,R4.2] V3:[R1.1,R2.1,R3.1,R4.1]` | identical |
| **signal across three sheets** | 3 | `GND:[R1.2..R6.2] SIG:[R1.1..R6.1]` | identical |
| **repeated block** | 2 | `A_TAP:[R1.2,R2.1] B_TAP:[R3.2,R4.1] GND:[R2.2,R4.2] V3:[R1.1,R3.1]` | identical |

**THE REPEATED-BLOCK FIXTURE WAS REWRITTEN, AND THAT IS THE PART WORTH A LATER READER'S TIME.** Its
first version put each instance's two resistors in ONE block, which made each tap INTERNAL to its
block. An internal net is not labelled (`labelledNets`, `ir/classify.ts`), so neither tap crossed
anything, KiCad named them `Net-(R1-Pad2)` and `Net-(R3-Pad2)` in both exports, and **the case
could not have detected a cross-sheet name collision at all** - the thing the spec says it is for.
Splitting each instance across two blocks on two sheets makes both taps labelled crossing nets, and
they survive as `A_TAP` and `B_TAP` with two members each.

**AND THE COMPARISON IS OF PARTITIONS, NOT OF NAMES.** KiCad names an unlabelled net after a pad it
touches, so a name is a fact about designators. `partitionOf` discards the names and compares the
set of member sets, which is the claim §1.6 makes.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 15, Steps 1-4.
- **Evidence** the table above, printed from the two `importNetlist` results per case. A check that
  could have failed: the comparison also asserts the partition has more than one net, so an export
  with nothing in it cannot pass by being trivially equal; and the first fixture version failed the
  named-tap assertion, which is how the defect above was found rather than argued.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer wrote the fixtures, ran the exports and read the netlists.
- **Why it is open** it is a measurement. It stays because it is the only evidence anyone has that
  the cross-sheet mechanism behaves, and because the rewritten fixture records a way to write this
  test that proves nothing.
- **What would settle it** nothing. **A caution:** all three fixtures are `rail-row` blocks of
  two-terminal passives, chosen so they reach KiCad without the ELK backend. The test says nothing
  about a circuit whose blocks ELK draws.

### G205 - SEAM B's CHOICE RULE FOR A NEGOTIABLE POSITION, and the consequence that `fixed` and `negotiable` differ today in exactly one thing: what `AttachedPort.was` reports

Spec §1.9 and plan decision **D9** both leave open *"how seam B chooses among negotiable
positions"*. Task 15 owns that choice. What `composeBlocks` implements:

> **An interface port attaches at the block's own `Anchor` for that net, translated by the offset
> the packing gave its frame, and nowhere else. A declared side the anchor's position within the
> block's own extent does not put it on is a refusal, not an instruction to move it.**

**ROUND 2 CORRECTED THE SECOND SENTENCE, AND THE CORRECTION IS G210's.** Round 1 compared the
anchor's `side` - a DIRECTION its glyph points - against the declaration's EDGE. It now derives
the edge from the anchor's position within `anchorExtent(layout)` (`edgesOfAnchor`), a corner
lies on two edges and satisfies either, and `pinSideOfAnchor` is deleted rather than replaced.

**THE REASON IS §1.9's OWN CONTRACT AND NOT A SHORTAGE OF IMAGINATION.** An `Anchor` is where a
block's layout brings a net to its boundary, and the wire that reaches it is inside the block.
Attaching the net anywhere else means re-routing that wire - which §1.9 forbids by name, *"it does
not re-route a wire inside one"* - or adding a second wire, which would be a connection the IR does
not have.

**SO THE FREEDOM `negotiable` GRANTS IS REAL AND THIS IMPLEMENTATION DECLINES TO USE IT.** `[RAN]`
Over the five blocks the ELK backend draws, composing with the shelf packing and with the ELK
packing puts every one of the ten interface ports at a different absolute position and at **the
same offset from its own frame's origin**, with the same side and the same net - so the set of
`(block, net, side, was)` is identical under the two packings. **A port's position is a function of
its block and of nothing on the page.**

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 15, Step 5.
- **Evidence** `tests/schgen/render/compose.test.ts`'s *"the same ports come back at the same places
  whichever packer placed the frames"*, which first asserts the two packings' frame positions
  DIFFER - so the agreement below is not two runs of one packing - and then compares the attached
  sets. And *"a fixed interface position is honoured, not relocated"*, which recomputes each
  expected point from the block's own anchor and the frame offset independently of what
  `composeBlocks` returned.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer wrote the rule, the module and the tests and ran them.
- **Why it is open** it is a decision recorded so it can be disputed, and **it has a consequence an
  implementer would otherwise get wrong**: reading `negotiable` as *"seam B will place this for
  you"* is false of this generator. The two values differ only in what `was` reports and in whether
  the declaration is a true claim (**G206**).
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: seam B either exercises the freedom `negotiable` grants, or
  the declaration stops claiming it.** **MECHANISMS, both untried:** (1) let a block declare more
  than one acceptable anchor per net and have seam B pick among them, which needs a renderer that
  produces alternatives and none does; (2) drop `negotiable` from `InterfacePort` and make every
  port of a drawn block `fixed`, which is `CLAUDE.md`'s *supersede means delete* applied to a field
  nothing varies - and which would be wrong for a block that has not been drawn yet.

### G206 - RE-MEASURED: the declared split is still 0 fixed / 51 negotiable, and for the 10 ports of the 5 blocks that now DRAW, `negotiable` is a false claim in the other direction

**G153** measured 51 interface ports, 0 fixed and 51 negotiable, and judged the zero sound on an
explicit ground: *"a block with no geometry has none to fix a port against"*, every block being
`{ kind: "auto" }` with no template. **Five blocks now have geometry** (**G200**), so that premise
no longer holds for them and the figure was re-taken rather than inherited.

**THE DECLARED SPLIT IS UNCHANGED.** `[RAN]` `bun tools/schgen/authoring-census.ts`: 12 declared
blocks, **51 interface ports, 0 fixed, 51 negotiable** - identical to G153's table, because no
authoring file was edited and `negotiablePort` is still what every one of them calls.

**THE MEASURED ANSWER IS DIFFERENT FOR FIVE BLOCKS, AND THEY ARE ALL `transistor-preamp`'s.**

| block | interface ports | draws | anchors drawn for those ports | positions seam B could choose among |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tp-leg-upper` | 2 | yes | `VCC` up, `BASE` right | 1 each |
| `tp-leg-feedback` | 2 | yes | `COLLECTOR` right, `BASE` right | 1 each |
| `tp-leg-lower-a` | 2 | yes | `BASE` right, `GND` down | 1 each |
| `tp-leg-lower-b` | 2 | yes | `BASE` right, `GND` down | 1 each |
| `tp-leg-collector` | 2 | yes | `VCC` up, `COLLECTOR` right | 1 each |
| the other seven | 41 | no | none | - |

**Each of those ten nets has exactly ONE anchor, at one position, put there by the block's own
layout.** §1.9 defines `fixed` as *"a position fixed by the block's own internal geometry"*, and
under **G205**'s choice rule seam B cannot move one without re-routing a wire inside the block. **So
all ten are genuinely fixed and all ten are declared negotiable.** The remaining 41 belong to
blocks with no geometry, where `negotiable` is still the only true claim.

**AND THE DECLARATION OVERSTATES THE FREEDOM VISIBLY IN SIX OF THE TEN.** `BASE` and `COLLECTOR` are
declared `sides: [left, right]` - two acceptable edges - and the geometry permits exactly one.

**ROUND 2: THE FALSE CLAIM IS NOT ONLY IN `position`, AND THE OTHER HALF IS IN THE FIELD §1.9
MAKES CARRY IT.** `negotiablePort` generates a `why` ending *"The position within that edge is
seam B's, because this block declares no template and so has no internal geometry to fix it."*
**That sentence is false for all ten of these ports**: the block has internal geometry, it is
drawn, and the position is fixed by it. `InterfacePort.why` is required non-blank precisely
because a position is a claim, so a stale `why` is the same defect as a stale `position` and is
the one a reader meets first.

**G153's THUMB ON THE SCALE IS DOING WORK HERE, AND ROUND 1's "it did not cause this" IS
WITHDRAWN.** There is no `fixedPort` anywhere and `negotiablePort` is the only helper; **17 files
call it**, and `tests/schgen/__fixtures__/composed.ts` synthesises the whole of `mini`'s 33-port
interface through it. So it is not merely that a later writer will meet the asymmetry: **every
port in every measurement in G205, G206 and G210 is produced by that one helper's rule rather
than by an authored declaration**, with a single exception (`mini`'s `FLASH` `3V3`, declared as a
literal at round 2). One helper, one rule, and no second way to write a port.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 15, Step 5a.
- **Evidence** the census output for the declared half; for the measured half, `blockContent` run
  over all twelve blocks with the real ELK backend, printing each drawn layout's anchors (the table
  above is that output). A check that could have failed: `tests/schgen/render/compose.test.ts`'s
  *"a fixed interface position is honoured"* re-declares all ten ports `fixed` and composes, and
  every attached point equals the block's own anchor translated - so "fixed" is reachable and
  behaves, and the 0 in the census is a property of the declarations.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer ran the census, the per-block layout dump and the tests.
- **Why it is open** the declarations now carry a claim the geometry contradicts for five blocks,
  and nothing refuses it.
- **What would settle it** **CRITERION: a block that has been drawn declares `fixed`, with a true
  `why`, for every interface port its layout gives exactly one anchor.**
  **AND ROUND 1's PROPOSED MECHANISM IS WITHDRAWN AS AN INVERSION, which is the part of this
  entry a later reader most needs.** It proposed comparing each declared `position` against the
  anchors **the block's realised ELK layout draws**. For these five blocks that makes the agent's
  own artifact the criterion for the declaration the artifact is judged against - `CLAUDE.md`'s
  governing invariant, wearing a measurement's clothes. **The legitimate sources for an authored
  `fixed` and its `sides` are the ones already reviewed:** the part's own library pin sides
  (`pinSidesFor` / `sideOfPin`, read off the symbol's `(at x y angle)`), or, for a block that
  declares a template, that template's anchor. **Reading a side off a reviewed ported template is
  reading someone else's artifact and is fine; reading it off the backend under test is not.**
  **MECHANISM, untried, under that constraint:** derive the candidate sides from the symbol's own
  pin geometry and refuse a declaration that names an edge no pin of the block's boundary net sits
  on - which needs the symbols, so it belongs in `authoring-checks.ts` and not in seam B.

### G207 - BOTH PACKINGS MEASURED, SIDE BY SIDE, WITH NO PREFERENCE EXPRESSED - and the first thing the numbers say is that no packing changes how much ink is on the page

**G165**'s criterion (b) - *"a sheet whose frames use a small fraction of the declared paper is
either reported or packed better"* - **deliberately refuses to let an implementer decide what
"better packing" means**, because *"better" there is an acceptance criterion for an artifact an
agent produces*. That refusal binds Task 15. So: a second packer exists, both are measured, and
**the comparison stands undecided.**

`[RAN]` `packFramesWithElk` against `packFrames`, over the two sheets of the ported `mini` design
and over a probe of the five `transistor-preamp` blocks that draw:

| sheet | packer | extent (mm) | aspect | usable aspect | page use | extent fill | inter-frame span |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mini/power` A4, 4 frames | shelf | 185.42 x 38.10 | 4.87 | 1.85 | 17.8 % | 78.4 % | - (0 edges) |
| | elk | 109.22 x 71.12 | 1.54 | 1.85 | 19.5 % | 71.3 % | - (0 edges) |
| `mini/signal` A3, 7 frames | shelf | 358.14 x 55.88 | 6.41 | 1.69 | 21.7 % | 56.4 % | 820.42 mm / 8 edges |
| | elk | 245.11 x 127.00 | 1.93 | 1.69 | 33.8 % | 36.3 % | 656.59 mm / 8 edges |
| tp probe A3, 5 frames | shelf | 248.92 x 40.64 | 6.13 | 1.69 | 11.0 % | 91.4 % | 305.44 mm / 4 edges |
| | elk | 203.20 x 81.28 | 2.50 | 1.69 | 17.9 % | 56.0 % | 248.28 mm / 4 edges |

**THE INK IS IDENTICAL AND NO PACKING CAN CHANGE IT.** Frame area over usable area is 13.9 %,
12.3 % and 10.0 % on the three, **the same for both packers**, because `frameSize` is a property of
the blocks. **So G165's complaint that *"the page is mostly empty"* is only partly a packing
question**: the content occupies a tenth to a seventh of the usable area whatever is done with it,
and what a packer moves is the SHAPE of the region it occupies, the fraction of the page that
region spans, and the distance between connected frames.

**WHAT THE ELK PACKER IS PACKING TO.** The aspect ratio it is given is the paper's own usable area
(`elk.aspectRatio`), the spacings and the padding are `pack.ts`'s own `GAP`, `MARGIN` and
`TITLE_BLOCK`, and `elk.layered.wrapping.strategy = MULTI_EDGE` is what makes `layered` honour an
aspect ratio at all. **Why the unconstrained wrapping strategy is this writer's stated rule and not
a reviewed one**: a wrapped edge normally costs a long connector, and here an inter-frame edge is
**drawn as nothing** (**G208**), so a cut costs no ink and `SINGLE_EDGE`'s restriction would
constrain the wrap for a cost this drawing does not pay. A later reader may dispute it.

**THE TWO PAGES WERE LOOKED AT, and this paragraph is an OBSERVATION FOR THE RECORD and NOT AN
ACCEPTANCE** - §3.3 gives these measures no threshold and G165's criterion (b) is the owner's. Both
`mini` signal pages were exported with `kicad-cli` at 150 dpi and read. The shelf page is one row of
seven frames across the top fifth of an A3, read strictly left to right, input connector first and
output connector last, with four-fifths of the page blank. The ELK page is three bands cascading
down and right: the two frames with no inter-frame edge at all (the spare op-amp channel and the
op-amp supply) are pushed into the leftmost layer, **ahead of the input connector**, and the
crystal sits above the output connector rather than beside it. **This writer would rather read the
shelf page**, for a reason that is about reading order rather than area: a schematic sheet read as a
single left-to-right row needs no decision about where to look next, and the ELK page's first
column is two blocks that connect to nothing. **That is a preference, it is recorded as one, and it
is the owner's to accept or reject** - the brief for this task says in terms that a preference found
here *is the finding*.

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 15, Step 6.
- **Evidence** the table, computed by `packingMeasures` over both packings of each content list; two
  PDFs exported through `kicad-cli sch export pdf --theme schgen`, converted with
  `pdftoppm -r 150 -png` and read with the Read tool. A check that could have failed:
  `tests/schgen/elk/sheet-graph.test.ts`'s *"BOTH packings are measured and NEITHER is preferred
  here"* asserts the two extents DIFFER and the two ink figures AGREE, so a packer that silently
  returned the other's positions would fail it.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer ran both packers, exported, converted and read both pages.
**ROUND 2: THE ELK PACKING IS IN PRODUCTION WHILE THE QUESTION IS OPEN, AND THAT BELONGS IN THIS
ENTRY RATHER THAN ONLY IN A REPORT.** `generate` runs `sheetPackPrePass` -> `packSheet`, and the
selection rule - stated once, in `tools/schgen/elk/sheet-layout.ts`, and mandated by Task 15's
brief - sends any sheet with an inter-frame edge to ELK. **So `mini`'s signal sheet now emits as
the ELK page: the page this entry records a preference against.** That is not a rule violation -
the brief required the mechanical selection - but *"the shipped page changed shape to the one the
writer would rather not read, and nobody has ruled on (b)"* is exactly the state this entry
exists to carry, and round 1 left it in a report that `.superpowers/` gitignores.

- **Why it is open** G165's criterion (b) is unanswered and this entry does not answer it. It adds
  the numbers the decision needs and one reader's preference, both of which were missing. **And
  the decision now has a shipped artifact riding on it.**
- **What would settle it** **an OWNER DECISION**, which is what G165 says. The numbers above are
  what there is to decide on. **If the answer is "report it rather than pack it better", the
  change is one line in `packSheet` and the ELK packer stays as a measured alternative.**

### G208 - MEASURED: seam B draws NO wire and adds NO crossing, so §1.1's 6.1x upper bound is not spent on seam B's own geometry at all - what composition costs is glyphs and page area

Spec §1.1's third limit, carried into Task 15's brief: both spikes drew each block *"on its own
canvas, so the totals add crossings across three sheets and seam B would add its own"*. **Seam B's
own crossings had never been measured.** They have now, and the answer is zero, for a structural
reason rather than a lucky one.

**EVERY WIRE ON A COMPOSED SHEET BELONGS TO EXACTLY ONE BLOCK.** `layoutSheet` builds its wire list
as `a.blocks.flatMap((b) => b.layout.wires)` and adds none of its own, and every inter-block
connection is represented by a power symbol or a global label (**G203**) drawn at the block's own
anchor, which was already inside that block's extent before composition. `[RAN]` On the composed
`mini` signal sheet, **every one of the 39 wires lies inside exactly one frame's box, and no two
frame boxes overlap.**

**WHAT COMPOSITION DOES COST, measured on the two subjects:**

| subject | blocks | interface ports attached | inter-frame edges | inter-frame span | wire length seam B added | crossings seam B added |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mini/signal` | 7 frames | 25 declared, 6 of them REFUSED so the composition does not complete (**G210**) | 8 over 8 nets | 656.59 mm (elk) / 820.42 mm (shelf) | **0** | **0** |
| tp 5-block probe | 5 | 10 of 10 | 4 over 2 nets (`BASE` spans 4 frames, `COLLECTOR` 2) | 248.28 mm (elk) / 305.44 mm (shelf) | **0** | **0** |

**"Inter-frame span" is a Manhattan centre-to-centre distance and NOT a wire length**, deliberately:
no line joins two frames, so what it measures is how far a reader's eye travels between the two ends
of one global label. It is the quantity a connectivity-aware packer can shorten, and the only one.

**WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT §1.1, carried with revision 4's framing.** 6.1x is a measured **upper bound**
on the improvement, not an estimate of it, and this figure is how much of it seam B spends: **none
of it in crossings.** The decomposition's 43 missing edges (139 whole against 96 in three blocks,
**G100**) do not come back as sheet-level crossings in this generator; they come back as **declared
interface ports drawn as glyphs inside their own blocks**, which were counted in the block's own
drawing already. **The cost that remains is page area and eye-travel, not ink.**

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 15, Step 5a.
- **Evidence** the table; `tests/schgen/render/compose.test.ts`'s *"spec §3.4 on a composed sheet"*,
  which asserts **both endpoints** of every wire fall inside exactly one frame box and that the
  drawing has wires at all, so the zero is not an empty-set pass. (**Round 1 tested only endpoint
  `a`**, which is weaker than the claim this entry carries; the review confirmed the claim true for
  both before it was strengthened.) A further check that could have failed: a point outside every
  frame is reported as held by none. For the frame disjointness, `frameBoxOverlaps` over both
  packings of all three content lists, with a driven case that reports an overlap and a driven case
  of two frames that merely touch and reports none.
- **Verified** CONFIRMED - this writer ran every figure.
- **Why it is open** it is a measurement Task 17 needs. **It is also bait, and the trap is named
  here**: "seam B adds no crossings" is true of THIS generator because this generator joins blocks
  with labels rather than with wires. A later change that drew an inter-block wire would make every
  number above wrong, and it would not be a defect in anything this entry measured.
- **What would settle it** nothing - it is a measurement. **A caution for Task 17 Step 4:** the
  comparison against the flat baseline must compare like with like, and the flat drawing has no
  frames and no interface glyphs at all.

### G209 - composition leaves G200's two numbers EXACTLY unchanged, and the staircase measure is vacuous at sheet scale - so it must keep being taken per block

**G200** measures, over the five blocks that draw, **14 placements with 14 distinct x-coordinates
(0 parts sharing an x)** and **9 of 19 nets reversing direction on an axis (47 %)**, and records
them as *"the baseline any attempt is measured against"*. Task 15's brief asks what composition does
to them.

**IT DOES NOTHING TO EITHER, AND THE REASON IS A THEOREM RATHER THAN LUCK.** `[RAN]` Over the same
five blocks, composed onto one A3 by the shelf packer and by the ELK packer: **14 placements, 14
distinct x, 19 wired nets, 9 reversing, 67 segments, 284.48 mm of wire - under both packers, and
identical to G200's table.** Composition translates each block by one rigid grid-multiple offset
(`translateLayout`), `interiorDrift` is empty, and **every quantity G200 measures is invariant under
translation**: a shared x stays shared, a reversal stays a reversal, a segment keeps its length.

**AND THE MEASURE MUST NOT BE RE-TAKEN AT SHEET SCALE, which is the part a later reader needs.**
Taken over a whole composed sheet it is vacuous: the frames sit at different x, so parts in
different blocks never share one whatever the renderer did. `[RAN]` The `mini` signal sheet - **every
block of which is drawn by a reviewed TEMPLATE** - gives **11 symbols and 11 distinct x**, which is
the same "staircase" verdict G200 reports for ELK and means nothing about either. **The number is a
property of a block's interior and only of that.**

- **Found** 2026-10-20, Task 15, Steps 5 and 6.
- **Evidence** the per-block tally above, computed over the composed layouts under both packings,
  beside G200's own table; and the sheet-scale tally over `mini/signal`. **ROUND 2 PUT THE

  failed: `tests/schgen/render/compose.test.ts`'s *"composition never alters a block's interior,
